This is **not** a ruling that derived data is out of scope for deletion; it is an unmodelled area, recorded so its absence is not mistaken for a decision. mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** Decide how one DAO interface serves PostgreSQL, CockroachDB and SQLite: per-driver
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-5",
  "summary": "Rule the multi-database abstraction shape",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Decide how one DAO interface serves PostgreSQL, CockroachDB and SQLite: per-driver implementations behind one interface, a single implementation with dialect branches, or codegen (sqlc). The existing recommendation in `multi-db-strategy.md` had been reached by one agent reading sources and never attacked, and codegen had been name-checked without ever being argued. Run as a three-hats debate; ruling and all three positions in `decisions/multi-db-abstraction.md`. Outcome: per-driver confirmed — but the document's stated reason was wrong and is corrected in place. Of the six concerns in its own dialect table, exactly two survive as real conditionals, so the two options cost roughly the same and the choice is reviewability, not cost. Codegen proved orthogonal to the question rather than a competing option: sqlc generates per-engine Queriers satisfying no common interface, so it fills the boxes per-driver implementations draw. It is left to 03 as an implementation preference.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] The receiving track can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning.\n- [x] The ruling names which option was chosen, on what grounds, and states plainly that the grounds are reviewability rather than cost.\n- [x] All three positions preserved verbatim, not summarized into agreement.\n- [x] Every correction to the prior document is visible as a correction, not a silent edit.\n- [x] Pattern footer records model per seat and hire turns consumed.\n- [x] Enforcement site for the ruling named: package boundaries, plus the conformance suite in Story 3 without which the ruling does not hold.\n\n**Depends on:** none. **Blocks:** Story 2 and Story 3 (this track).\n**Model/effort:** opus/high (lead synthesis) + 3× sonnet (debate seats)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 1 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-05",
      "no-code-yet"
    ]
  }
}

The existing recommendation in `multi-db-strategy.md` had been reached by one agent reading sources and never attacked, and codegen had been name-checked without ever being argued. Run as a three-hats debate; ruling and all three positions in `decisions/multi-db-abstraction.md`. Outcome: per-driver confirmed — but the document's stated reason was wrong and is corrected in place. Of the six concerns in its own dialect table, exactly two survive as real conditionals, so the two options cost roughly the same and the choice is reviewability, not cost. Codegen proved orthogonal to the question rather than a competing option: sqlc generates per-engine Queriers satisfying no common interface, so it fills the boxes per-driver implementations draw. It is left to 03 as an implementation preference.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n- [x] The receiving track can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning.\n- [x] The ruling names which option was chosen, on what grounds, and states plainly that the grounds are reviewability rather than cost.\n- [x] All three positions preserved verbatim, not summarized into agreement.\n- [x] Every correction to the prior document is visible as a correction, not a silent edit.\n- [x] Pattern footer records model per seat and hire turns consumed.\n- [x] Enforcement site for the ruling named: package boundaries, plus the conformance suite in Story 3 without which the ruling does not hold.\n\n**Depends on:** none. **Blocks:** Story 2 and Story 3 (this track).\n**Model/effort:** opus/high (lead synthesis) + 3× sonnet (debate seats)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 1 — done.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10154","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"Refinement","id":"10154","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/2","id":2,"key":"new","colorName":"blue-gray","name":"To Do"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-14"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"claude-code","toolName":"createJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"37ca82f0-5afb-4975-9642-9d559303645b","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}
mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** `Search()` is the flagship query of the DAO contract and the only genuinely open de
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-5",
  "summary": "Settle the Search() query shape",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** `Search()` is the flagship query of the DAO contract and the only genuinely open design question in it — every other method is fixed by the assignment text. Settle the `ProfileQuery` field set, per-field match semantics, filter combination, pagination form, sort order and stability, what `total` counts, and how the documented SQLite parity gap surfaces to a caller. Run as an adversarial pair; ruling and all objections in `decisions/search-query-shape.md`. Eight numbered objections raised, eight accepted, none declined. Four were live defects: `ORDER BY name` returning different page-1 rows per backend (PostgreSQL collation vs. SQLite `BINARY` byte order); `LOWER(name) LIKE` unable to use a GIN index declared on the bare column, so the accelerator accelerated nothing; caller input reaching a `LIKE` pattern unescaped; and `Country` normalized into the query but not into the table.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] The receiving track can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning.\n- [x] Every objection closes with an explicit \"what would change my mind\"; every one answered in writing, with declines stated rather than silent.\n- [x] Each caller-visible guarantee names its enforcement site — collation clause in DDL plus `ORDER BY` expression plus conformance test; expression index with the textual-match rule; DAO-side escaping plus `ESCAPE '\\'`; `CHECK` constraint plus write-side normalization.\n- [x] A guarantee deliberately not made is also recorded with its site as \"none — accepted\" (no index supports the ordering; every `Search` sorts its filtered set).\n- [x] Pattern footer records model per seat and hire turns consumed.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 1. **Blocks:** Story 3.\n**Model/effort:** opus/high (lead ruling) + 2× sonnet (Proposer, Skeptic)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 2 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-05",
      "no-code-yet"
    ]
  }
}

mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** Turn the prose strategy in `multi-db-strategy.md` into a contract 03 can implement
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-5",
  "summary": "Deliver the Go-shaped DAO contract to track 03",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Turn the prose strategy in `multi-db-strategy.md` into a contract 03 can implement without re-deriving this track's reasoning: interface signatures, a per-method summary table, domain types, the full sentinel set with translation rules, field-level schema with nullability per backend family, indexes, and a numbered out-of-scope list. `security-graded` because it specifies credential storage — `secret`, `secret_state`, `hash_algo`, `hash_cost` — which falls under 02's independent second-review rule. Includes the factory-shape resolution agreed directly with 03 (`dao.Repository` as a composite exposing `Profiles()`/`Credentials()`/`Methods()`, keeping `dao.New(driver, dsn)` unchanged; kept an interface so 03 can mock it) and the write-path retry seam required by `research-cockroachdb-postgres-semantics.md`. Reviewed by 03's own Detail Hawk after delivery; four findings accepted, one of which added `CreateProfileWithCredential` — the contract had barred 03 from composing a cross-call transaction while supplying no atomic path for registration, leaving a window where a profile exists with PII and no credential.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] 03 can implement without re-deriving the reasoning — verified by 03 reading it cold and confirming, not asserted by the author.\n- [x] Every caller-visible guarantee names its enforcement site; the two weakest sites (`is_active`, and `requires_secret` ↔ `secret_state`, both unable to be DDL constraints because `CHECK` cannot reference another table) are named as weakest rather than quietly listed.\n- [x] Nullability stated per column, per backend family, with \"absent\" single-valued: NULL means absent, `''` is invalid, enforced by named `CHECK` constraints.\n- [x] Error sentinels enumerated with trigger conditions; translation by structured error codes plus constraint names defined in our own DDL, never message text.\n- [x] Out-of-scope list numbered, each item naming why and whom to flag.\n- [x] Counter-intuitive behaviours warned before a reader meets them.\n- [x] Contract carries no `.go` or `.sql` file — Go-shaped prose only.\n\n**Depends on:** Stories 1, 2, 6. **Blocks:** 03's DAO implementation story (title TBD — 03's backlog); 04's migration-execution work via Story 5.\n**Model/effort:** opus/high — asymmetric risk: a wrong nullability or interface signature propagates into 03 and 04 and is expensive to reverse (`../02-ai-security-architecture/planning-approach.md` §1)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 3 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-05",
      "security-graded",
      "no-code-yet"
    ]
  }
}

mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** Test the contract against the hand-off standard this track asked the project to ado
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-5",
  "summary": "Cold-read the 05→03 hand-off and fix what fails",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Test the contract against the hand-off standard this track asked the project to adopt, using a reader deliberately kept unfamiliar with the track's reasoning. The hire was instructed at spawn not to read `multi-db-strategy.md`, `pii-governance.md` or the research docs, and sat out two debates to remain a usable instrument; she declared her one contamination (`PLAN.md` told her what the contract intended to contain) unprompted and reported against text rather than intent. Result in `decisions/handoff-legibility-05-03.md`: 14 blocking items against a contract three other reviewers had already passed; all 14 accepted and fixed, plus three tail findings adopted. A parallel cold read of `migration-approach.md` by a hire on loan from 04 ran alongside.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] Reader is genuinely cold; the restriction and its cost are recorded, and any contamination declared.\n- [x] Every finding either fixed or recorded with a reason for declining; none declined here.\n- [x] Surprise-versus-warning audit performed for each counter-intuitive behaviour, with placement corrected where a reader met the surprise first.\n- [x] Jargon undefined on first use catalogued and defined.\n- [x] Cross-track consequences of legibility gaps traced — a `pg_trgm` glossary gap had already propagated into a missing migration-runner credential row in 04's secrets inventory.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 3 (drafted). **Blocks:** Story 3 (closing) — deliberately circular: the cold read gates the contract being called stable.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet (cold reader) + opus/high (revisions)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 4 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-05",
      "no-code-yet"
    ]
  }
}

none declined here.\n* \\[x\\] Surprise-versus-warning audit performed for each counter-intuitive behaviour, with placement corrected where a reader met the surprise first.\n* \\[x\\] Jargon undefined on first use catalogued and defined.\n* \\[x\\] Cross-track consequences of legibility gaps traced — a `pg_trgm` glossary gap had already propagated into a missing migration-runner credential row in 04's secrets inventory.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 3 (drafted). **Blocks:** Story 3 (closing) — deliberately circular: the cold read gates the contract being called stable.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet (cold reader) + opus/high (revisions)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 4 — done.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10154","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"Refinement","id":"10154","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/2","id":2,"key":"new","colorName":"blue-gray","name":"To Do"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-17"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"claude-code","toolName":"createJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"3d0f452a-e202-46f9-8a56-6cbbd8f7460a","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}

input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-5",
  "summary": "Set PII retention windows and the deletion mechanism",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** `pii-governance.md` previously stated the policy shape and stopped at \"a product/legal decision this track doesn't own outright\" — true, and not actionable: 04 cannot build a sweep against a principle. This story puts proposed numbers in a table and specifies the mechanism they plug into. Windows: 24 months for `source='direct'`, 30 days for `idp_cache`, 7 days for orphaned cache rows, and no independent window for `user_credential` (wholly governed by its profile via the cascade FK). Every basis cell is either an engineering rationale or the honest word *unknown* — there is no third kind, because storage limitation under GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) is a principle demanding a justified window, not a number anyone can look up, and a citation implying otherwise would be a false statement in a client-facing document. Adds a `deletion_log` table to the schema, PII-free by construction, `profile_id` deliberately carrying no FK because the row it names is meant not to exist.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] 04 can build the sweep without re-deriving the reasoning.\n- [x] Every proposed number marked as a POC default pending a product/legal ruling; unknown bases and ratifiers left visibly empty rather than filled with plausible citations.\n- [x] Orphan rows keyed on `created_at`, not `updated_at` — a clock the read path touches lets a row reset its own expiry and never die.\n- [x] The cache window documented as \"since last use\", not \"since first seen\", with its relationship to the orphan rule stated as one rule seen from two sides.\n- [x] Both cascade consequences stated loudly: deleting a profile destroys its credentials; deleting a credential does not delete the profile, so a user removing their last login method still has PII on the `direct` clock. Named as a product decision that is currently not what the schema does.\n- [x] Deletion is hard, not soft-flagged; subject deletion reuses the sweep's code path; `deletion_log` holds no PII, with a conformance test asserting it.\n- [x] Health check specified as a requirement: rows examined, rows deleted, and age of the oldest surviving row per class — the third being the only signal that detects a silently stopped sweep, since rows-deleted cannot distinguish a broken sweep from an empty one.\n\n**Depends on:** none. **Blocks:** Story 6; 04's retention-sweep and observability work (title TBD — 04's backlog; already folded into their `observability.md`).\n**Model/effort:** sonnet (author) + opus/high (ruling)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 5 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-05",
      "security-graded",
      "no-code-yet"
    ]
  }
}

input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-5",
  "summary": "Deliver the migration approach to track 04",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** One of the three inputs 04 was gated on. `migration-approach.md` specifies the tool (goose), the three-directory layout with its two-invocation mechanism and separate version tables, the seed-data rule, and five requirements on 04 — migrations as a pre-start step, single-runner exclusion, fail-closed when the schema is behind, two distinct database credentials, and rollback not being a data-recovery plan. Put through a devil's-advocate objection turn (`decisions/migration-approach-objections.md`): six objections, six accepted. The most valuable overturned the reasoning behind the document's central requirement while leaving the requirement standing — R2 had argued the database cannot provide a lock because CockroachDB lacks advisory locks, a premise already corrected in this track's own research. The true reason is scope: a transaction-scoped lock releases between goose files and cannot cover a multi-file run, while session-scoped locks that would cover it are the ones CockroachDB does not support.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] 04 can act without re-deriving the reasoning — verified by a cold read from a 04 hire on loan, all findings fixed.\n- [x] Every requirement states whether it is a requirement (mechanism 04's choice) or a mechanism (and why the requirement cannot be met otherwise).\n- [x] Fail-closed checks both version tables, not one — checking only `shared/` would pass with the trigram index unapplied.\n- [x] Migration-runner and runtime credentials separated, with `CREATE EXTENSION` privileges named as PostgreSQL-only.\n- [x] Unverified facts left visibly open rather than asserted — whether goose's default version table carries a unique `version_id`, with a recommendation that does not depend on the answer.\n- [x] Tool-independence claim names its one exception rather than overclaiming.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 5 (`deletion_log` belongs in the shared migration series). **Blocks:** 04's migration-job and CI stages (title TBD — 04's backlog; \"provisional\" now dropped on their side).\n**Model/effort:** opus/high + sonnet (objection seat)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 6 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-05",
      "no-code-yet"
    ]
  }
}

input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-5",
  "summary": "Extend subject-deletion to derived data",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** A subject-deletion request currently reaches `user_profile` and, by cascade, `user_credential`. It does not reach derived data — application logs, metrics, connector traces, or anything else that may have incidentally captured a name, phone or address in transit. That data has no `source` column, no retention clock, and in most cases no primary key to select on. This is **not** a ruling that derived data is out of scope for deletion; it is an unmodelled area, recorded so its absence is not mistaken for a decision. Raised by this track's Spreadsheet hire against her own stated blind spot — everything else became a row because it fit a column, and this resisted the table.\n\n**Proposed resolution, offered rather than assumed:** the cheapest control is upstream of deletion entirely. If PII never enters a log, there is nothing to delete from it — which makes 02's never-log list the real control here, not a deletion job this track could specify. That argues for the enforcement site sitting with 02 (what may be logged) and 04 (log retention and where logs physically live), with 05 supplying only the definition of what counts as PII.\n\n**Acceptance criteria (draft — to be confirmed by the owning track)**\n- [ ] The enforcement site is named and owned by exactly one track, with the other two linked rather than assumed.\n- [ ] The decision records whether derived-data deletion is in scope, out of scope, or mitigated upstream — an explicit ruling either way, not continued silence.\n- [ ] If mitigated upstream, 02's never-log list names the PII fields from `multi-db-strategy.md` §5 explicitly rather than by category.\n- [ ] Whatever is decided is reachable from `pii-governance.md`, so the governance note does not imply a completeness it lacks.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 5. **Blocks:** nothing yet. **Linked:** 02 (never-log list), 04 (log retention).\n**Model/effort:** TBD with owner\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 7 — open.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-05",
      "security-graded",
      "no-code-yet",
      "from-consistency-pass"
    ]
  }
}

The existing recommendation in `multi-db-strategy.md` had been reached by one agent reading sources and never attacked, and codegen had been name-checked without ever being argued. Run as a three-hats debate; ruling and all three positions in `decisions/multi-db-abstraction.md`. Outcome: per-driver confirmed — but the document's stated reason was wrong and is corrected in place. Of the six concerns in its own dialect table, exactly two survive as real conditionals, so the two options cost roughly the same and the choice is reviewability, not cost. Codegen proved orthogonal to the question rather than a competing option: sqlc generates per-engine Queriers satisfying no common interface, so it fills the boxes per-driver implementations draw. It is left to 03 as an implementation preference.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n- [x] The receiving track can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning.\n- [x] The ruling names which option was chosen, on what grounds, and states plainly that the grounds are reviewability rather than cost.\n- [x] All three positions preserved verbatim, not summarized into agreement.\n- [x] Every correction to the prior document is visible as a correction, not a silent edit.\n- [x] Pattern footer records model per seat and hire turns consumed.\n- [x] Enforcement site for the ruling named: package boundaries, plus the conformance suite in Story 3 without which the ruling does not hold.\n\n**Depends on:** none. **Blocks:** Story 2 and Story 3 (this track).\n**Model/effort:** opus/high (lead synthesis) + 3× sonnet (debate seats)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 1 — done.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10157","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"Done","id":"10157","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/3","id":3,"key":"done","colorName":"green","name":"Done"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-14"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"claude-code","toolName":"transitionJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"47d8310a-e04a-4f5f-9c4e-8dcfd4427d95","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}

Settle the `ProfileQuery` field set, per-field match semantics, filter combination, pagination form, sort order and stability, what `total` counts, and how the documented SQLite parity gap surfaces to a caller. Run as an adversarial pair; ruling and all objections in `decisions/search-query-shape.md`. Eight numbered objections raised, eight accepted, none declined. Four were live defects: `ORDER BY name` returning different page-1 rows per backend (PostgreSQL collation vs. SQLite `BINARY` byte order); `LOWER(name) LIKE` unable to use a GIN index declared on the bare column, so the accelerator accelerated nothing; caller input reaching a `LIKE` pattern unescaped; and `Country` normalized into the query but not into the table.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[x\\] The receiving track can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning.\n* \\[x\\] Every objection closes with an explicit \"what would change my mind\"; every one answered in writing, with declines stated rather than silent.\n* \\[x\\] Each caller-visible guarantee names its enforcement site — collation clause in DDL plus `ORDER BY` expression plus conformance test; expression index with the textual-match rule; DAO-side escaping plus `ESCAPE '\\'`; `CHECK` constraint plus write-side normalization.\n* \\[x\\] A guarantee deliberately not made is also recorded with its site as \"none — accepted\" (no index supports the ordering; every `Search` sorts its filtered set).\n* \\[x\\] Pattern footer records model per seat and hire turns consumed.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 1. **Blocks:** Story 3.\n**Model/effort:** opus/high (lead ruling) + 2× sonnet (Proposer, Skeptic)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 2 — done.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10157","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"Done","id":"10157","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/3","id":3,"key":"done","colorName":"green","name":"Done"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-15"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"claude-code","toolName":"transitionJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"3b285031-d5b4-4df7-ad1b-3e37fd928646","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}

Turn the prose strategy in `multi-db-strategy.md` into a contract 03 can implement without re-deriving this track's reasoning: interface signatures, a per-method summary table, domain types, the full sentinel set with translation rules, field-level schema with nullability per backend family, indexes, and a numbered out-of-scope list. `security-graded` because it specifies credential storage — `secret`, `secret_state`, `hash_algo`, `hash_cost` — which falls under 02's independent second-review rule. Includes the factory-shape resolution agreed directly with 03 (`dao.Repository` as a composite exposing `Profiles()`/`Credentials()`/`Methods()`, keeping `dao.New(driver, dsn)` unchanged; kept an interface so 03 can mock it) and the write-path retry seam required by `research-cockroachdb-postgres-semantics.md`. Reviewed by 03's own Detail Hawk after delivery; four findings accepted, one of which added `CreateProfileWithCredential` — the contract had barred 03 from composing a cross-call transaction while supplying no atomic path for registration, leaving a window where a profile exists with PII and no credential.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[x\\] 03 can implement without re-deriving the reasoning — verified by 03 reading it cold and confirming, not asserted by the author.\n* \\[x\\] Every caller-visible guarantee names its enforcement site; the two weakest sites (`is_active`, and `requires_secret` ↔ `secret_state`, both unable to be DDL constraints because `CHECK` cannot reference another table) are named as weakest rather than quietly listed.\n* \\[x\\] Nullability stated per column, per backend family, with \"absent\" single-valued: NULL means absent, `''` is invalid, enforced by named `CHECK` constraints.\n* \\[x\\] Error sentinels enumerated with trigger conditions; translation by structured error codes plus constraint names defined in our own DDL, never message text.\n* \\[x\\] Out-of-scope list numbered, each item naming why and whom to flag.\n* \\[x\\] Counter-intuitive behaviours warned before a reader meets them.\n* \\[x\\] Contract carries no `.go` or `.sql` file — Go-shaped prose only.\n\n**Depends on:** Stories 1, 2, 6. **Blocks:** 03's DAO implementation story (title TBD — 03's backlog); 04's migration-execution work via Story 5.\n**Model/effort:** opus/high — asymmetric risk: a wrong nullability or interface signature propagates into 03 and 04 and is expensive to reverse (`../02-ai-security-architecture/planning-approach.md` §1)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 3 — done.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10157","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"Done","id":"10157","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/3","id":3,"key":"done","colorName":"green","name":"Done"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-16"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"claude-code","toolName":"transitionJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"86e04599-cc70-4bcc-8e35-b17e737921ad","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}

The hire was instructed at spawn not to read `multi-db-strategy.md`, `pii-governance.md` or the research docs, and sat out two debates to remain a usable instrument; she declared her one contamination (`PLAN.md` told her what the contract intended to contain) unprompted and reported against text rather than intent. Result in `decisions/handoff-legibility-05-03.md`: 14 blocking items against a contract three other reviewers had already passed; all 14 accepted and fixed, plus three tail findings adopted. A parallel cold read of `migration-approach.md` by a hire on loan from 04 ran alongside.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[x\\] Reader is genuinely cold; the restriction and its cost are recorded, and any contamination declared.\n* \\[x\\] Every finding either fixed or recorded with a reason for declining; none declined here.\n* \\[x\\] Surprise-versus-warning audit performed for each counter-intuitive behaviour, with placement corrected where a reader met the surprise first.\n* \\[x\\] Jargon undefined on first use catalogued and defined.\n* \\[x\\] Cross-track consequences of legibility gaps traced — a `pg_trgm` glossary gap had already propagated into a missing migration-runner credential row in 04's secrets inventory.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 3 (drafted). **Blocks:** Story 3 (closing) — deliberately circular: the cold read gates the contract being called stable.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet (cold reader) + opus/high (revisions)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 4 — done.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10157","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"Done","id":"10157","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/3","id":3,"key":"done","colorName":"green","name":"Done"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-17"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"claude-code","toolName":"transitionJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"1f90b5bc-6cb4-484a-a7de-bd4f00fd5eac","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}

{"issues":{"nodes":[{"expand":"renderedFields,names,schema,operations,editmeta,changelog,versionedRepresentations","id":"13256","self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/issue/13256","key":"LT-18","fields":{"summary":"Set PII retention windows and the deletion mechanism","issuetype":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/issuetype/10125","id":"10125","description":"","iconUrl":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/2/universal_avatar/view/type/issuetype/avatar/10315?size=medium","name":"Story","subtask":false,"avatarId":10315,"entityId":"cff7a49e-2156-4962-b5c6-1f2d09bd0e6d","hierarchyLevel":0},"project":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/project/10102","id":"10102","key":"LT","name":"LoginID-Test","projectTypeKey":"software","simplified":true,"avatarUrls":{"48x48":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/universal_avatar/view/type/project/avatar/10411","24x24":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/universal_avatar/view/type/project/avatar/10411?size=small","16x16":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/universal_avatar/view/type/project/avatar/10411?size=xsmall","32x32":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/universal_avatar/view/type/project/avatar/10411?size=medium"}},"description":"**Description.** `pii-governance.md` previously stated the policy shape and stopped at \"a product/legal decision this track doesn't own outright\" — true, and not actionable: 04 cannot build a sweep against a principle. This story puts proposed numbers in a table and specifies the mechanism they plug into. Windows: 24 months for `source='direct'`, 30 days for `idp_cache`, 7 days for orphaned cache rows, and no independent window for `user_credential` (wholly governed by its profile via the cascade FK). Every basis cell is either an engineering rationale or the honest word _unknown_ — there is no third kind, because storage limitation under GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) is a principle demanding a justified window, not a number anyone can look up, and a citation implying otherwise would be a false statement in a client-facing document. Adds a `deletion_log` table to the schema, PII-free by construction, `profile_id` deliberately carrying no FK because the row it names is meant not to exist.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[x\\] 04 can build the sweep without re-deriving the reasoning.\n* \\[x\\] Every proposed number marked as a POC default pending a product/legal ruling; unknown bases and ratifiers left visibly empty rather than filled with plausible citations.\n* \\[x\\] Orphan rows keyed on `created_at`, not `updated_at` — a clock the read path touches lets a row reset its own expiry and never die.\n* \\[x\\] The cache window documented as \"since last use\", not \"since first seen\", with its relationship to the orphan rule stated as one rule seen from two sides.\n* \\[x\\] Both cascade consequences stated loudly: deleting a profile destroys its credentials; deleting a credential does not delete the profile, so a user removing their last login method still has PII on the `direct` clock. Named as a product decision that is currently not what the schema does.\n* \\[x\\] Deletion is hard, not soft-flagged; subject deletion reuses the sweep's code path; `deletion_log` holds no PII, with a conformance test asserting it.\n* \\[x\\] Health check specified as a requirement: rows examined, rows deleted, and age of the oldest surviving row per class — the third being the only signal that detects a silently stopped sweep, since rows-deleted cannot distinguish a broken sweep from an empty one.\n\n**Depends on:** none. **Blocks:** Story 6; 04's retention-sweep and observability work (title TBD — 04's backlog; already folded into their `observability.md`).\n**Model/effort:** sonnet (author) + opus/high (ruling)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 5 — done.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10157","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"Done","id":"10157","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/3","id":3,"key":"done","colorName":"green","name":"Done"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-18"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"claude-code","toolName":"transitionJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"30696d5d-433c-475d-85cd-f6c6d3a4215b","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}

Put through a devil's-advocate objection turn (`decisions/migration-approach-objections.md`): six objections, six accepted. The most valuable overturned the reasoning behind the document's central requirement while leaving the requirement standing — R2 had argued the database cannot provide a lock because CockroachDB lacks advisory locks, a premise already corrected in this track's own research. The true reason is scope: a transaction-scoped lock releases between goose files and cannot cover a multi-file run, while session-scoped locks that would cover it are the ones CockroachDB does not support.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[x\\] 04 can act without re-deriving the reasoning — verified by a cold read from a 04 hire on loan, all findings fixed.\n* \\[x\\] Every requirement states whether it is a requirement (mechanism 04's choice) or a mechanism (and why the requirement cannot be met otherwise).\n* \\[x\\] Fail-closed checks both version tables, not one — checking only `shared/` would pass with the trigram index unapplied.\n* \\[x\\] Migration-runner and runtime credentials separated, with `CREATE EXTENSION` privileges named as PostgreSQL-only.\n* \\[x\\] Unverified facts left visibly open rather than asserted — whether goose's default version table carries a unique `version_id`, with a recommendation that does not depend on the answer.\n* \\[x\\] Tool-independence claim names its one exception rather than overclaiming.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 5 (`deletion_log` belongs in the shared migration series). **Blocks:** 04's migration-job and CI stages (title TBD — 04's backlog; {"issues":{"nodes":[{"expand":"renderedFields,names,schema,operations,editmeta,changelog,versionedRepresentations","id":"13258","self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/issue/13258","key":"LT-20","fields":{"summary":"Extend subject-deletion to derived data","issuetype":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/issuetype/10125","id":"10125","description":"","iconUrl":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/2/universal_avatar/view/type/issuetype/avatar/10315?size=medium","name":"Story","subtask":false,"avatarId":10315,"entityId":"cff7a49e-2156-4962-b5c6-1f2d09bd0e6d","hierarchyLevel":0},"components":[],"created":"2026-09-12T14:57:47.957-0700","description":"**Description.** A subject-deletion request currently reaches `user_profile` and, by cascade, `user_credential`. It does not reach derived data — application logs, metrics, connector traces, or anything else that may have incidentally captured a name, phone or address in transit. That data has no `source` column, no retention clock, and in most cases no primary key to select on. This is **not** a ruling that derived data is out of scope for deletion; it is an unmodelled area, recorded so its absence is not mistaken for a decision. Raised by this track's Spreadsheet hire against her own stated blind spot — everything else became a row because it fit a column, and this resisted the table.\n\n**Proposed resolution, offered rather than assumed:** the cheapest control is upstream of deletion entirely. If PII never enters a log, there is nothing to delete from it — which makes 02's never-log list the real control here, not a deletion job this track could specify. That argues for the enforcement site sitting with 02 (what may be logged) and 04 (log retention and where logs physically live), with 05 supplying only the definition of what counts as PII.\n\n**Acceptance criteria (draft — to be confirmed by the owning track)**\n\n* \\[ \\] The enforcement site is named and owned by exactly one track, with the other two linked rather than assumed.\n* \\[ \\] The decision records whether derived-data deletion is in scope, out of scope, or mitigated upstream — an explicit ruling either way, not continued silence.\n* \\[ \\] If mitigated upstream, 02's never-log list names the PII fields from `multi-db-strategy.md` §5 explicitly rather than by category.\n* \\[ \\] Whatever is decided is reachable from `pii-governance.md`, so the 1	# Track 04 — Infra & DevOps Backlog
2	
3	Track: 04-infra-devops. Lead: Theo Bergman. Epic: "Infra & DevOps: Containerization, CI/CD, and Operations" (key: TBD, team-lead fills in on transcription).
4	
5	Authored now per Phase 4; will be re-checked against the consistency pass's cross-cutting findings (`PLAN.md` §"Cross-cutting — enforcement sites") once that report lands, particularly for Story 6 below. All stories carry `no-code-yet` — Warren's Phase 4 go covers backlog authoring, not implementation; a separate, explicit code go-ahead is still required before any `.go`, Dockerfile, CI config, or compose file is written for real.
6	
7	## Story 1 — Containerize `api-service` and `idp-connector`
8	
9	**Description:** Build the two multi-stage Go images (distroless final stage, non-root, read-only root filesystem) and the Deployment/Service/NetworkPolicy manifests targeting the lab cluster, per `./containerization-design.md`. Covers both binaries' Dockerfiles, resource requests/limits sized per service (CPU-bound `api-service` vs. I/O-bound `idp-connector`), the migration `Job` (parallelism 1, gated by the CI pipeline's exclusivity mechanism, not Kubernetes ordering alone), a default-deny `NetworkPolicy` on `idp-connector` so its "no inbound Service" isolation claim actually holds against the namespace's default-allow network, and — per the consistency pass's F13 finding — a **third manifest**: `api-service-issuer`, a second Deployment of the same `api-service` image (`APP_MODE=issuer`) whose own ServiceAccount is the only one that mounts the JWT signing key, since RBAC on the `Secret` verb does nothing once it's volume-mounted into the verifying Deployment's replicas.
10	
11	**Acceptance criteria:**
12	- [ ] The receiving track (whoever implements/reviews this) can act on the manifests without re-deriving the reasoning in `containerization-design.md`.
13	- [ ] Both images build from a pinned Go version, produce a static binary, and contain nothing but the binary (+ CA certs for `idp-connector`) — enforcement site: multi-stage Dockerfile's final `COPY` list.
14	- [ ] Neither Pod can write to its own root filesystem at runtime — enforcement site: `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`.
15	- [ ] `idp-connector` is unreachable except from `api-service` — enforcement site: the `NetworkPolicy` ingress rule scoped to `api-service`'s pod selector.
16	- [ ] A stuck `idp-connector` cannot starve `api-service` if colocated on one node — enforcement site: `resources.limits` on both Pod specs.
17	- [ ] The migration `Job` cannot start a second concurrent run — enforcement site: the CI pipeline's concurrency-gated deploy stage (Story 3), not a database lock.
18	- [ ] The JWT signing private key is mounted into `api-service-issuer` only, never into `api-service`'s own Deployment — enforcement site: `api-service`'s manifest carries no volume/mount referencing that `Secret` at all, verified by manifest inspection, not RBAC.
19	
20	**Depends on:** 03 — `cmd/api-service` and `cmd/idp-connector` build as real binaries (service boundaries already stable, per `PLANNING.md`); 05 — final migration tooling name for the `Job`'s invocation (already final, `05-data-ops/migration-approach.md`).
21	
22	**Model/effort:** Sonnet, medium.
23	
24	**Type:** Story.
25	
26	**Labels:** `track-04`, `no-code-yet`.
27	
28	## Story 2 — Deliver secrets to both services per 02's inventory
29	
30	**Description:** Implement the Kubernetes-native `Secret` delivery mechanism in `./secrets-delivery.md`: file-mounted secrets keyed by name only in manifests, RBAC scoped per-service (and, for the JWT signing key, scoped to the issuing code path specifically, not `api-service`'s verification path), cluster-level encryption-at-rest for the `Secret` resource type, and the migration-runner credential's backend-specific provisioning (`CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm` rights on PostgreSQL only, nothing extra on CockroachDB, no privilege model on SQLite) kept distinct from the runtime service credential (DML-only, no DDL, per 05's R4).
31	
32	**Acceptance criteria:**
33	- [ ] 02 (the hand-off's author) confirms this implementation matches `handoff-04-secrets.md` v2's inventory without needing to re-explain any row.
34	- [ ] No `Secret` value appears in a manifest, image layer, build arg, or CI log — enforcement site: manifests reference names only; CI's `gitleaks` stage (Story 3).
35	- [ ] No ServiceAccount can `get`/`list` a `Secret` it doesn't mount — enforcement site: per-service `Role`/`RoleBinding` scoped to named `Secret`s.
36	- [ ] The migration-runner credential and the runtime service credential are provisioned as two distinct `Secret`s, never one — enforcement site: separate `Secret` objects, separate `Role`s, per 05's R4.
37	- [ ] `Secret` resources are encrypted at rest in etcd — enforcement site: cluster `EncryptionConfiguration`.
38	
39	**Depends on:** 02 — `handoff-04-secrets.md` (received, v2, final); 05 — `migration-approach.md` R4 (final).
40	
41	**Model/effort:** Sonnet, medium.
42	
43	**Type:** Story.
44	
45	**Labels:** `track-04`, `security-graded`, `no-code-yet`.
46	
47	## Story 3 — CI/CD pipeline: build, lint, test, scan, migrate, describe-only deploy
48	
49	**Description:** Stand up the pipeline in `./ci-pipeline.md`: build/lint/test(`-race`, three DB targets: SQLite, Postgres, CockroachDB)/security-scan/image-build on every PR; push-images/migration-job/describe-only-deploy on merge. The migration-job stage is where 05's R2 exclusivity requirement is actually enforced — a concurrency-gated pipeline stage, not a database lock, since no single lock mechanism covers both the right scope (session, to span `goose`'s per-file transactions) and the right engine (CockroachDB supports transaction-scope only).
50	
51	**Acceptance criteria:**
52	- [ ] A developer or reviewer can act on this pipeline description without re-deriving why each stage exists.
53	- [ ] A lint or test failure blocks merge — enforcement site: required-status-check on the PR, not advisory.
54	- [ ] A CockroachDB-specific SQL incompatibility surfaces at PR time, not deploy time — enforcement site: the dedicated CockroachDB testcontainer job.
55	- [ ] Only one migration run can reach the migrate stage at a time, across concurrent deploys — enforcement site: the pipeline's own concurrency group/mutex on the deploy environment.
56	- [ ] No secret enters a build log or image layer — enforcement site: `gitleaks` stage plus the Dockerfile's minimal `COPY` list (Story 1).
57	- [ ] The final deploy stage is documented (which manifests, which namespace, which credential) but not invoked — enforcement site: stage exists as a named, non-executing step until a separate real-deploy decision is made.
58	
59	**Depends on:** 03 — test-strategy outline for `go test ./...` to run against; 05 — `migration-approach.md` (final).
60	
61	**Model/effort:** Sonnet, medium.
62	
63	**Type:** Story.
64	
65	**Labels:** `track-04`, `no-code-yet`.
66	
67	## Story 4 — Local dev-loop: compose profiles for SQLite and Postgres
68	
69	**Description:** Build the `docker-compose.yml` in `./local-dev-loop.md`: `sqlite` and `postgres` profiles matching 03's `DB_DRIVER` env var, a mock/local `idp-connector` target, hot-reload (`air`) for `api-service` in dev profiles only, and local-only dev credentials clearly distinguished from the real secrets mechanism (Story 2).
70	
71	**Acceptance criteria:**
72	- [ ] A new developer can run either profile from this file alone, without asking what `DB_DRIVER` values are valid.
73	- [ ] The `postgres` profile exercises the shared `postgres`-package code path (Postgres + CockroachDB) — enforcement site: compose service definition wiring `DB_DRIVER=postgres`.
74	- [ ] Dev credentials never appear in `./secrets-delivery.md`'s mechanism or in any real manifest — enforcement site: explicit statement in the file plus separate variable naming (`dev`/`dev`, hardcoded client id/secret).
75	- [ ] Hot-reload has zero effect on the production image build — enforcement site: `air` target scoped to compose dev profiles only, never `./containerization-design.md`'s Dockerfile.
76	
77	**Depends on:** 03 — `DB_DRIVER`/config-surface env vars (already stable, per `PLANNING.md`).
78	
79	**Model/effort:** Sonnet, low.
80	
81	**Type:** Story.
82	
83	**Labels:** `track-04`, `no-code-yet`.
84	
85	## Story 5 — Observability: logging, metrics, never-log enforcement, retention-sweep alerting
86	
87	**Description:** Implement `./observability.md`: structured `slog` logging with an explicit-field discipline (never a whole request/response struct through a log call), a lint check flagging never-log-list field names, RED metrics with no PII-cardinality labels, ingress-level query-string redaction for search endpoints, RBAC-separated audit-log read access, and 05's S5 retention-sweep requirement — rows-examined/rows-deleted/oldest-surviving-row-age metrics per data class, with an alert when oldest-row-age exceeds retention-window-plus-sweep-interval, since a dead sweep job produces zero rows-deleted either way and gives no other symptom.
88	
89	**Acceptance criteria:**
90	- [ ] 02 confirms the never-log list (`handoff-04-secrets.md`'s nine items) is fully covered by a named enforcement site, not just a policy statement.
91	- [ ] No password, token, JWT, client secret, or DSN reaches a log call — enforcement site: explicit-field logging discipline plus the CI lint check.
92	- [ ] Search-endpoint name/phone query fragments never appear in ingress access logs — enforcement site: ingress log-format override / redaction.
93	- [ ] Audit-log read access is a distinct RBAC grant from Secret-read access — enforcement site: separate `Role` bound to an incident-review group.
94	- [ ] A stopped retention-sweep job triggers an alert within one sweep interval of its window being exceeded — enforcement site: the `oldest_surviving_row_age_seconds` alert rule, per data class.
95	
96	**Depends on:** 02 — `handoff-04-secrets.md`'s never-log list (final); 05 — `pii-governance.md` S5 retention numbers and data-class names (final).
97	
98	**Model/effort:** Sonnet, medium.
99	
100	**Type:** Story.
101	
102	**Labels:** `track-04`, `security-graded`, `no-code-yet`.
103	
104	## Story 6 — Configure log-sink retention for the audit trail
105	
106	**Description:** The consistency pass (`../decisions/cross-track-consistency.md`, "Deletion gap") ruled the enforcement site: a subject-deletion request reaches `user_profile`/`user_credential` by cascade but not application logs, metrics, or the audit trail, none of which has a `source` column or a deletion hook. 02's never-log list is the upstream control (PII values never enter a log in the first place, per `./observability.md`'s enforcement mechanism), which leaves exactly one remaining artifact needing a retention window: the audit trail itself (`sub`, scope, opaque record id, timestamp) — pseudonymous, not PII-free, and after a profile deletion the only remaining record that a given record id was looked up by a given caller. The enforcement site for its expiry is a retention policy on the log sink 04 already operates (Loki or equivalent, per `./observability.md`'s "Audit-log access" section) — not a deletion job, not a DAO method. 05 adds one row to `pii-governance.md`'s retention table for the audit-log window (basis: unknown, pending legal); 02 adds the two vocabulary/list fixes the pass identified for the never-log list (driver-error detail, `username`). This story configures the sink's retention setting to that window once it's a number.
107	
108	**Acceptance criteria:**
109	- [ ] The hand-off standard: 02 and 05 can each confirm their half (never-log list scope; retention-table row) without needing this story rewritten.
110	- [ ] The audit-log stream expires no later than 05's stated window — enforcement site: the log sink's retention configuration (a Loki `retention_period` or equivalent for the chosen sink), not application code.
111	- [ ] The retention configuration is separate from, and does not touch, any other log stream's retention or any Secret-access RBAC (`./secrets-delivery.md`) — enforcement site: sink-level retention is scoped per log stream/index, not global.
112	- [ ] Confirmed this is a configuration value, not a deletion job: no new DAO method, no new `cmd/` entrypoint, no scheduled job beyond what `./observability.md`'s retention-sweep story (Story 5) already covers for `user_profile`/`user_credential`-derived data.
113	
114	**Depends on:** 02 — never-log list additions (driver-error detail, `username`) confirmed; 05 — `pii-governance.md` audit-log retention-window row (basis: unknown, pending legal, per the pass).
115	
116	**Model/effort:** Sonnet, low.
117	
118	**Type:** Story.
119	
120	**Labels:** `track-04`, `from-consistency-pass`, `no-code-yet`.

Ran the ratified red/blue pattern (S1) against the IDP connector's vendor-token handling in `connector-security.md` §1: Tomasz Wrede's ranked top-five attack leaves, Felix Adebayo's alternatives turn (deleting two leaves by design change — no-cache-by-default rather than an encrypted, TTL-bound cache), Helena Marsh's blue response, Tomasz's rebuttal turn (closing a connection-reuse variant and tightening the accepted-replay-risk boundary). Full record: `decisions/connector-token-lifecycle-redblue.md`; attack-tree table appended to `connector-security.md`. This is the requirement set 03's connector implementation builds against directly.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[x\\] The receiving track (03) can implement the connector's token handling without re-deriving this run's reasoning — confirmed by Renata Cole directly.\n* \\[x\\] \"No persistent token cache by default\" — enforcement site: the connector's HTTP client construction, one fetch-per-`/identity`-call code path, no cache read/write call in the default path.\n* \\[x\\] \"Fresh, isolated `Authorization` header per outbound request\" — enforcement site: the outbound HTTP client factory used for vendor calls, explicitly not sharing a request-context object across calls.\n* \\[x\\] \"Fetch → use → zeroize, retries re-fetch\" — enforcement site: the token variable's scope inside the single vendor-call function; a retry path that calls `/auth` again rather than reusing a held token.\n* \\[x\\] Residual risk (bearer-token replay, accepted) is named in the artifact, not left implicit.\n\n**Depends on:** S1.\n**Model/effort:** opus, high for the connector's token-lifecycle implementation specifically (per `planning-approach.md` §1); sonnet, high for this track's design/debate turns.\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S3 — done.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10154","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"Refinement","id":"10154","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/2","id":2,"key":"new","colorName":"blue-gray","name":"To Do"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-23"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"claude-code","toolName":"createJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"6dd634bc-ddaa-4ca3-9523-ea1adf89ca55","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}
mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** Ran the adversarial pair pattern against `api-auth-design.md`'s scope sketch: Helen
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-2",
  "summary": "Adversarial pair: search-API authorization scoping",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Ran the adversarial pair pattern against `api-auth-design.md`'s scope sketch: Helena Marsh (Proposer) drafted the final scope vocabulary, `profile:search` provisioning bar, object-level policy hook, and pagination/rate-limit/lifecycle rules; Ingrid Solano (Skeptic) raised five numbered objections, each with a \"what would change my mind\" line; Helena revised all five. Full record: `decisions/search-authz-scoping.md`; finalized design folded into `api-auth-design.md`. This is the scope model 03's middleware and object-level policy checks implement directly.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] `profile:read:own` referral constraint — enforcement site: `authorize(sub, scope, target)` checking the `caller_referral` mapping, called in-handler before the DAO call.\n- [x] `profile:read:any` requires a `reason_code` from a closed enum on every call — enforcement site: request validation inside the same `authorize()` call, rejecting a missing or out-of-enum value.\n- [x] `profile:search` result-cap rejection (not truncation) — enforcement site: query-construction code in the search handler, checked before the DB call executes.\n- [x] Cursor-based pagination, page ceiling 50 — enforcement site: pagination-parameter validation in the handler layer.\n- [x] Per-client rate limits (60/10 req/min) and the cumulative distinct-record-touch counter, applying to `read:any` regardless of `reason_code` presence — enforcement site: rate-limiting middleware plus a counting store keyed per client credential, incremented per distinct record id returned.\n- [x] Scope-grant lifecycle (90-day backstop, immediate revocation on offboarding/idle/function-change) — enforcement site: whatever identity-lifecycle signal 03/04 wire the grant-issuing component to consume.\n\n**Depends on:** S1.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high (middleware and policy-check implementation); sonnet, high for this track's debate turns.\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S4 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-02",
      "security-graded"
    ]
  }
}

mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** Debated whether this project's multi-agent, persona-driven workflow produces better
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-2",
  "summary": "Structured written debate: ai-workflow-narrative.md's core claim",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Debated whether this project's multi-agent, persona-driven workflow produces better design than a single strong session, or is cost without evidence. Felix Adebayo (Position A) argued from two concrete instances (S3's design-deleting alternatives turn, 04's Newcomer cold-read catches); Ingrid Solano (Position B) rebutted that n=2 from roles built to find exactly this isn't evidence of a general law, and that null results (a clean concession in S3) must be counted alongside hits. Ruled per point in `decisions/ai-workflow-claim-debate.md`: against a general empirical claim, for a narrower mechanism-level one. Result folded into `ai-workflow-narrative.md` (S9).\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] Both positions preserved in the record, not just the winning one.\n- [x] The ruling states which position won on which point and why (per the `CASTING.md` §5 ⟨02⟩ amendment this story itself ratified in S1).\n- [x] The narrative (S9) states the mechanism-level claim, not the broader statistical one Position B defeated.\n\n**Depends on:** none.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S5 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-02"
    ]
  }
}

mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** Synthesized S4's ruling and the token-shape decisions in `api-auth-design.md` into
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-2",
  "summary": "Hand-off 02→03: auth scheme, validation point, authz requirements",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Synthesized S4's ruling and the token-shape decisions in `api-auth-design.md` into a receiver-shaped hand-off Renata Cole can build against without re-deriving this track's reasoning: token scheme, where it's validated, the final scope vocabulary and object-level policy hook, pagination/rate-limit numbers, the audit-log field list, and an explicit \"not yours to decide\" list. Revised to v2 after S8's independent review surfaced two implementation-relevant fixes (the decomposition counter's scope-coverage gap; the connector's own inbound-auth requirement). Accepted by 03 with a confirmed `authorize()` placement (in-handler, not middleware) and `DB_DSN_FILE` folded into the config surface.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] Receiving track (03) can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning in `api-auth-design.md`/`connector-security.md` — confirmed by Renata directly, cold read \"clean.\"\n- [x] Token TTL (5–15 min), no refresh, no denylist — enforcement site: `exp` claim check in the verification middleware; absence of a refresh-grant or denylist-lookup code path.\n- [x] Verifier pins expected algorithm, rejects `alg: none`/downgrade — enforcement site: explicit algorithm allow-list parameter on the JWT verification call.\n- [x] Public-key-only verification in `api-service`; private key isolated to the issuing code path — enforcement site: Kubernetes RBAC Role (per `handoff-04-secrets.md` row #2) plus code-level separation between issuing and verifying functions.\n- [x] `idp-connector`'s own `/auth`/`/identity` require authentication with a distinct audience/scope — enforcement site: the same JWT middleware pattern applied to `idp-connector`'s router, configured with `aud: idp-connector-service`.\n- [x] Token-endpoint brute-force protection — enforcement site: rate limiter on the token-issuing endpoint, keyed by `client_id` + source IP.\n- [x] Audit-log field list (`sub`, scope, record id, `reason_code`, policy decision, timestamp, outcome) and nothing beyond it — enforcement site: a single structured-logging call at the end of each search/retrieve handler, not scattered `log.Printf` calls a reviewer has to hunt for.\n\n**Depends on:** S4.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high (lead synthesis, no new hire turns); sonnet, high for 03's implementation against it.\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S6 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-02",
      "security-graded"
    ]
  }
}

mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** Authored the secrets inventory and never-log list Theo Bergman's track needs to des
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-2",
  "summary": "Hand-off 02→04: secrets inventory and never-log list",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Authored the secrets inventory and never-log list Theo Bergman's track needs to design secrets delivery against, then ran Ingrid Solano's single objection turn and folded in all four accepted objections: the authorization-server's ownership was mis-scoped by omission, a KMS-access credential row was missing, the `DB_DSN` env-var exception was too weak, and audit-log read access needed its own RBAC line distinct from Secret access. Cold-read by 04's Newcomer (Wesley Okonkwo) caught two further gating gaps (TOTP/token-cache feature-status ambiguity; a non-self-contained trust-boundary reference), both fixed.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] Receiving track (04) can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning in `threat-model.md`/`api-auth-design.md`/`connector-security.md` — confirmed by 04's Newcomer cold read, two gating items fixed before acceptance.\n- [x] `DB_DSN_FILE` required as the primary delivery mechanism, `DB_DSN` a transitional fallback — enforcement site: the config-loading code in `internal/config`, preferring the file path when both are set.\n- [x] JWT signing private key file-mount only, RBAC-restricted to the issuing code path's service account — enforcement site: the Kubernetes Role scoping `get`/`list` on that Secret.\n- [x] Client secrets stored hashed (Argon2id), never plaintext at rest — enforcement site: the provisioning code path that writes the hash, per `threat-model.md` Asset 1.\n- [x] One `Secret` per vendor registration (ABC/XYZ never share a Secret) — enforcement site: the Kubernetes manifest's per-vendor Secret object.\n- [x] Never-log list (vendor password, vendor token, PII values, raw vendor error bodies, signing key, JWTs, client secrets, `DB_DSN`, full `/auth`/`/identity` bodies, PII-bearing query params) — enforcement site: a log-formatting/redaction layer that structurally cannot emit these fields, not a code-review convention alone.\n- [x] Audit-log read access is a distinct, narrower grant than Secret-read access — enforcement site: log-pipeline RBAC or a separate log-sink access control, 04's mechanism.\n\n**Depends on:** one Skeptic objection turn (no debate pattern).\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high (lead synthesis + one hire turn).\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S7 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-02",
      "security-graded"
    ]
  }
}

input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-2",
  "summary": "Independent second review of the security-graded documents",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Ran an independent second-review pass on `threat-model.md`, `api-auth-design.md`, and `connector-security.md`, each reviewed by a hire who neither authored nor blue-teamed it. Required a mid-run reassignment: the original static roster assigned Helena Marsh to review two documents she'd since authored content in (S4's Proposer role, S3's blue seat) — caught and corrected before running, not after. Result: Helena reviewed `threat-model.md` (4 citation/precision fixes, 1 completeness note), Tomasz Wrede reviewed `api-auth-design.md` (4 findings, including a decomposition-counter gap that made a rate limit a silent no-op for `profile:read:any`), Ingrid Solano reviewed `connector-security.md` (2 findings — no auth requirement on inbound calls to the connector; no stated assumption about what a vendor token authorizes). All ten findings accepted, zero declined. Full record: `decisions/second-review-security-docs.md`.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] Every reviewer is verified independent (did not author or blue-team the document) at the moment the review runs, not just at planning time.\n- [x] Every accepted finding is fixed in the source document, not just recorded in the decision file.\n- [x] The two findings affecting 03's implementation (decomposition-counter scope, connector inbound-auth requirement) are propagated into `handoff-03-auth.md` v2 and relayed directly to 03.\n- [x] Null results (documents/findings that didn't surface anything) are counted in the tally alongside hits, not silently omitted.\n\n**Depends on:** S3, S4.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S8 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-02",
      "security-graded"
    ]
  }
}

  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",

  "summary": "Revise ai-workflow-narrative.md for the org layer",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Rewrote the AI-tooling narrative to cover what actually ran once hiring began: the persona/pattern-catalog layer this project built on top of Anthropic's documented orchestrator-worker pattern, honestly measured evidence from S3/S8 (including null results, not just hits), S5's ruling stated plainly with the losing position preserved, the S8 independence-reassignment lesson generalized (\"independence is checked at review time, not assigned once\"), and the real external operator agent named as deliberately out of scope and never contacted.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] Distinguishes what's Anthropic-documented from what this project composed on its own (unchanged discipline from the original draft).\n- [x] States the S5 ruling including the position that lost, not just the one that won.\n- [x] Leads with the single most concrete example (Tomasz's `profile:read:any` decomposition-counter finding) rather than an abstract summary.\n- [x] Names the external operator agent and states plainly it was never contacted.\n\n**Depends on:** S3, S4, S5, S8.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S9 — done.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-02"
    ]

}

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-2",
  "summary": "Independent review of 03's auth middleware and connector token code",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Once 03 implements the auth middleware (S6) and the connector's token-lifecycle code (S3), this track runs an independent code-level review of the security-graded surfaces only: token validation, the `authorize()` object-level policy hook, rate-limiting/decomposition-counter enforcement, and the connector's fetch-use-zeroize discipline. Reviewer assignment will be checked for independence at run time per the S8 lesson (whoever reviews must not have authored the code or the design doc it implements) rather than assumed from the current roster, since roles may have accumulated further authorship by then.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [ ] Reviewer independence verified at run time, not assumed from this backlog's authorship snapshot.\n- [ ] Every enforcement site named in S3/S4/S6/S7's acceptance criteria above is checked against the actual implementation, not just the design doc.\n- [ ] Findings recorded in `decisions/second-review-implementation.md`, following the same accept/decline-with-reason discipline as S8.\n- [ ] Any Residual **H** finding (per the S1 attack-tree convention) produces a follow-up story or a stated accepted risk, not a silent gap.\n\n**Depends on:** Warren's code go-ahead; 03's implemented auth middleware and connector token-lifecycle stories.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S11 — open.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-02",
      "security-graded",
      "no-code-yet"
    ]
  }
}

mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** The pass caught a real contradiction: `handoff-04-secrets.md` said the JWT signing
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-2",
  "summary": "Split the token issuer into an isolated Deployment",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** The pass caught a real contradiction: `handoff-04-secrets.md` said the JWT signing private key \"never touches `api-service`\" while also defining the issuer as \"a mode of `api-service`,\" and 04's manifest resolved that by mounting the signing key into every replica of a single `api-service` Deployment — RBAC on a Secret's `get` verb does nothing to stop a volume already mounted into a running container. Fixed at the design level in `handoff-04-secrets.md` Assumption 2 and row 2: the issuer runs as a second Deployment of the same `api-service` image, selected by an environment variable (`APP_MODE=issuer` vs. default), with its own ServiceAccount that alone mounts the signing-key Secret. This story is the implementation and manifest work that design change requires — it did not exist as a story before the pass.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [ ] `api-service` supports an `APP_MODE` environment variable selecting issuer vs. verifying behavior from one binary/image.\n- [ ] Two Kubernetes Deployments exist, each with its own ServiceAccount; only the issuer Deployment's pod spec mounts the JWT signing-key Secret — enforcement site: the manifest's volume mounts plus RBAC Role scoping `get`/`list` to the issuer's ServiceAccount.\n- [ ] The verifying Deployment's pod spec contains no reference to the signing-key Secret at all (not just RBAC-denied — physically absent from its mounts).\n- [ ] `containerization-design.md`'s mount at the lines the pass named is removed and replaced with the two-Deployment shape.\n\n**Depends on:** `handoff-04-secrets.md` v2 (this track); 03's `APP_MODE` config surface addition; 04's manifest change.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high (03 implementation); sonnet, high (04 manifest).\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S12 — open.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-02",
      "security-graded",
      "from-consistency-pass",
      "no-code-yet"
    ]
  }
}

mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_Rovo__createJiraIssue **Description.** Two related gaps the pass found: (1) nothing said what our own `/auth` returns to i
input
{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "projectKey": "LT",
  "issueTypeName": "Story",
  "parent": "LT-2",
  "summary": "Wire api-service's client credential for the connector call",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "description": "**Description.** Two related gaps the pass found: (1) nothing said what our own `/auth` returns to its caller or how `/identity` obtains vendor authority, given the assignment's fixed `/identity` body has no credential field (F3) — resolved in `connector-security.md` §1: `/auth` returns the vendor token to the authenticated internal caller, which presents it as a request header (not body field) on the subsequent `/identity` call; the connector itself still never caches it. (2) `api-service` needs its own client credential to authenticate to the connector's now-required inbound auth (`connector-security.md` §5) in the first place, and no inventory row covered it — added as row 10 in `handoff-04-secrets.md` (F15). This story is the implementation work both design fixes require.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [ ] `api-service` obtains and presents a `connector:identity-lookup`-scoped token (via its own client credential, row 10 of `handoff-04-secrets.md`) when calling `idp-connector`'s `/auth` and `/identity`.\n- [ ] The onboarding flow's vendor-auth step receives the vendor `access_token` from our `/auth` response and holds it only for the span between that call and the following `/identity` call — enforcement site: the handler/service layer that mediates the onboarding flow, not the connector itself (which remains stateless per S3).\n- [ ] `/identity` accepts the vendor token as a request header, not a body field, and fails closed with a generic error if it is missing or rejected by the vendor.\n- [ ] `01-product-industry-research-design/ux-notes.md`'s two-screen flow and this mechanism agree on what the frontend/onboarding-flow layer actually holds between screens (coordinate directly with Naomi if the UX description needs a one-sentence update to match).\n\n**Depends on:** `connector-security.md` (this track); `handoff-04-secrets.md` row 10 (this track); 03's connector-client implementation.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S13 — open.",
  "additional_fields": {
    "labels": [
      "track-02",
      "security-graded",
      "from-consistency-pass",
      "no-code-yet"
    ]
  }
}
