Fixed by adding two composite-level methods in `multi-db-strategy.md` §3c: `DeleteExpired(ctx, class, olderThan) (SweepResult, error)` and `DeleteProfile(ctx, id, reason, externalRef)`, both writing `deletion_log` in the same transaction as the delete. `SweepResult` returns rows examined, rows deleted, and the age of the oldest surviving row — the last being the only signal that detects a silently stopped sweep, since rows-deleted cannot distinguish a broken sweep from an empty one.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[x\\] Both methods sit on the composite, not on a sub-repository — they span `user_profile` and `deletion_log`, and the DAO is the only layer permitted to open a transaction.\n* \\[x\\] One retention class per call; never a mixed-class predicate.\n* \\[x\\] Each class uses its own clock column — `created_at` for orphans, because a clock the read path touches lets a row reset its own expiry.\n* \\[x\\] `OldestSurvivingAt` returned from the DAO rather than left for 04 to compute, since only the DAO can answer it in the same query plan.\n* \\[x\\] `Profiles().Delete` deliberately still writes no log row, with the reason recorded.\n* \\[x\\] The complete set of cross-table operations is stated as three; a fourth requires a contract change.\n* \\[x\\] 03 accepted the addendum after a Detail Hawk first-pass review that raised four findings, all accepted: `OldestSurvivingAt`'s nil case narrowed to \"class is empty\" only; `RetentionClass` zero value given an explicit conformance assertion; `reason` removed as a parameter on `DeleteProfile` and asserted by the method; and `DeleteExpired` bounded by a required `maxRows` with one transaction per batch, plus a never-request-scoped-context requirement.\n* \\[x\\] An interaction between two of those fixes, raised by neither, caught at ruling: batching makes deletable rows remain mid-sweep by construction, so `OldestSurvivingAt` would be old on every batch but the last and would fire the alert every run. It is therefore meaningful only when `Drained` is true. Relayed to 04 so the alert rule is drained-gated.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 3 (LT-16), Story 5 (LT-18). **Blocks:** 03's S11 — the sweep-invocation and subject-deletion-request code that calls `DeleteExpired`/`DeleteProfile` and surfaces `OldestSurvivingAt` to 04's observability (LT-44).\n**Model/effort:** opus/high (contract addendum) + sonnet (03's first-pass review)\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 8 — done.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10157","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"Done","id":"10157","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/3","id":3,"key":"done","colorName":"green","name":"Done"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-50"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"claude-code","toolName":"transitionJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"e70a2014-f5e9-4825-8bc7-2717b667e699","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}

1	# Backlog — 01 Product & Industry Research (incl. Design)
2	
3	**Track:** `01-product-industry-research-design/` **Lead:** Naomi Voss **Epic:** LT-1
4	
5	All seven items below are **already done** — this track closed all six `PLAN.md` stories plus its housekeeping task before Phase 4 opened. Per team-lead's instruction, a story whose acceptance criteria are already met is created and closed as done; that is the honest backlog for a design/prose track with no implementation step of its own; every "Model/effort" below reflects what actually produced the work, not a future estimate.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Story 1 — Audit every claim in the framing/rationale docs for evidence (LT-6)
10	
11	**Description:** Audit every quantitative or evaluative claim in `industry-framing.md`, `personas-use-cases.md`, and `api-connector-design-rationale.md` against this track's two research passes (`research-loginid-company.md`, `research-oauth-history.md`), then fix or soften every unsupported claim in place. Precondition for Story 2 — the structured written debate needs to argue over claims that have already been checked, not claims that might not survive scrutiny. Produced by Desmond Okafor (Spreadsheet archetype, claims-auditor seat), synthesized by the lead.
12	
13	**Acceptance criteria:**
14	- [x] The receiving reader (evaluator, or another track citing this doc) can act on every remaining claim without re-deriving whether it's sourced.
15	- [x] `decisions/claims-audit.md` exists with a claim / source / status / resolution row for every quantitative or evaluative claim in the three docs.
16	- [x] Every claim marked asserted/unsourced in the audit is either softened in place or has a named evidence file — no claim ships at a confidence level the audit didn't support. Enforcement site: the edits themselves in `industry-framing.md` and `personas-use-cases.md`, cross-checked against the audit table.
17	
18	**Depends on:** — (first-wave, no upstream dependency)
19	**Model/effort:** sonnet, medium (Spreadsheet-archetype hire; synthesis by lead)
20	**Type:** Task
21	**Labels:** `track-01`, `no-code-yet`
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Story 2 — Resolve whether the password baseline is a deliberate framing choice or an over-read (LT-7)
26	
27	**Description:** Run a structured written debate — Position (Imogen Hale, Storyteller) argues the password/legacy-connector baseline is worth narrating as a deliberate "before/after" simplification; Rebuttal (Tobias Lindqvist, Designated Skeptic) argues that's an unfalsifiable claim about the assignment author's intent; Desmond Okafor fact-checks both; the lead synthesizes. This is the one genuinely contestable framing decision in the track, and it's binding for `industry-framing.md` §2/§4 and for the one-paragraph thesis the final submission packet uses.
28	
29	**Acceptance criteria:**
30	- [x] Another track or an evaluator can read `industry-framing.md` §2/§4 and act on the framing without re-opening the debate itself.
31	- [x] `decisions/password-baseline-debate.md` preserves the full Position, Rebuttal, fact-check, and synthesis — both positions kept in the record, not only the winning one.
32	- [x] Every claim about what the assignment "is testing for" or what LoginID "intended" is removed or explicitly hedged as a stated belief, not an assertion — the synthesis's ruling, applied directly to `industry-framing.md`. Enforcement site: the revised document text itself (no residual first-person-certainty phrasing about evaluator/author intent).
33	
34	**Depends on:** Story 1 (must run over already-checked claims)

118	## S7. Auth middleware (JWT validation) (LT-40)
119	
120	**Description:** The middleware at the `cmd/api-service` edge validating the client-credentials JWT scheme from `handoff-03-auth.md` v3 — public-key-only verification, `sub`/`scope`/`exp`/`iat`/`aud` claim checks, `kid`-based key rotation, no denylist (TTL-only revocation, a deliberate trade-off not to be re-litigated). Also covers the `APP_MODE=verifier|issuer` split (`PLANNING.md`) — this Deployment mode never mounts the signing key regardless of `APP_MODE`'s value, since `verifier` is this story's own code path and `issuer` is a separate mode of the same binary the F13 fix depends on to keep the two isolated by Deployment, not just by RBAC.

123	- [ ] Implements 02's token scheme without re-deriving the no-refresh/no-denylist reasoning in `api-auth-design.md`.
124	- [ ] Rejects any token whose `aud` doesn't match this service's audience — enforcement site: the claim-validation step, with a unit test using a mismatched-audience token.
125	- [ ] Verifies with the public key only; the private signing key never touches this binary's code path — enforcement site: dependency/import check (no signing-key material referenced in `internal/api`).
126	- [ ] **Pins the expected signing algorithm and rejects any token whose header claims a different one**, including `alg: none` and a symmetric-algorithm downgrade using the public key as an HMAC secret (RFC 8725 §3.1) — enforcement site: explicit algorithm check in the JWT verification call, not left to the library's default (`handoff-03-auth.md` v3 names this as a common library footgun).
127	- [ ] The token-issuing endpoint (the `APP_MODE=issuer` mode) has its own failed-grant rate limiting and progressive backoff per `client_id` and per source IP, separate from the resource-API limits below, with alerting on a sustained run of failed grants against one `client_id` — enforcement site: issuer-mode middleware, distinct from the verifier-mode rate limiter (`handoff-03-auth.md` v3).
128	- [ ] Per-client-credential rate limits (60 req/min read, 10 req/min search) and the cumulative distinct-record-touch counter (rolling 24h) are enforced and alert on sustained near-limit usage, not just throttle — enforcement site: the rate-limit middleware plus its own test.
129	- [ ] The deadline budget for a request (context propagation into the DAO layer) is sized to cover realistic p99 DAO latency, per `decisions/context-propagation.md`'s ruling — stated as a concrete number in this story's implementation, not left as "some deadline."
130

7	## Story 1 — Containerize `api-service` and `idp-connector` (LT-45)
8	
9	**Description:** Build the two multi-stage Go images (distroless final stage, non-root, read-only root filesystem) and the Deployment/Service/NetworkPolicy manifests targeting the lab cluster, per `./containerization-design.md`. Covers both binaries' Dockerfiles, resource requests/limits sized per service (CPU-bound `api-service` vs. I/O-bound `idp-connector`), the migration `Job` (parallelism 1, gated by the CI pipeline's exclusivity mechanism, not Kubernetes ordering alone), a default-deny `NetworkPolicy` on `idp-connector` so its "no inbound Service" isolation claim actually holds against the namespace's default-allow network, and — per the consistency pass's F13 finding — a **third manifest**: `api-service-issuer`, a second Deployment of the same `api-service` image (`APP_MODE=issuer`) whose own ServiceAccount is the only one that mounts the JWT signing key, since RBAC on the `Secret` verb does nothing once it's volume-mounted into the verifying Deployment's replicas.
10	
11	**Acceptance criteria:**
12	- [ ] The receiving track (whoever implements/reviews this) can act on the manifests without re-deriving the reasoning in `containerization-design.md`.
13	- [ ] Both images build from a pinned Go version, produce a static binary, and contain nothing but the binary (+ CA certs for `idp-connector`) — enforcement site: multi-stage Dockerfile's final `COPY` list.
14	- [ ] Neither Pod can write to its own root filesystem at runtime — enforcement site: `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`.
15	- [ ] `idp-connector` is unreachable except from `api-service` — enforcement site: the `NetworkPolicy` ingress rule scoped to `api-service`'s pod selector.
16	- [ ] A stuck `idp-connector` cannot starve `api-service` if colocated on one node — enforcement site: `resources.limits` on both Pod specs.
17	- [ ] The migration `Job` cannot start a second concurrent run — enforcement site: the CI pipeline's concurrency-gated deploy stage (Story 3), not a database lock.
18	- [ ] The JWT signing private key is mounted into `api-service-issuer` only, never into `api-service`'s own Deployment — enforcement site: `api-service`'s manifest carries no volume/mount referencing that `Secret` at all, verified by manifest inspection, not RBAC.
19	
20	**Depends on:** 03 — `cmd/api-service` and `cmd/idp-connector` build as real binaries (service boundaries already stable, per `PLANNING.md`); 05 — final migration tooling name for the `Job`'s invocation (already final, `05-data-ops/migration-approach.md`).

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "issueIdOrKey": "LT-16",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "fields": {
    "description": "**Description.** Turn the prose strategy in `multi-db-strategy.md` into a contract 03 can implement without re-deriving this track's reasoning: interface signatures, a per-method summary table, domain types, the full sentinel set with translation rules, field-level schema with nullability per backend family, indexes, and a numbered out-of-scope list. `security-graded` because it specifies credential storage — `secret`, `secret_state`, `hash_algo`, `hash_cost` — which falls under 02's independent second-review rule. Includes the factory-shape resolution agreed directly with 03 (`dao.Repository` as a composite exposing `Profiles()`/`Credentials()`/`Methods()`, keeping `dao.New(driver, dsn)` unchanged; kept an interface so 03 can mock it) and the write-path retry seam required by `research-cockroachdb-postgres-semantics.md`. Reviewed by 03's own Detail Hawk after delivery; four findings accepted, one of which added `CreateProfileWithCredential` — the contract had barred 03 from composing a cross-call transaction while supplying no atomic path for registration, leaving a window where a profile exists with PII and no credential.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] 03 can implement without re-deriving the reasoning — verified by 03 reading it cold and confirming, not asserted by the author.\n- [x] Every caller-visible guarantee names its enforcement site; the two weakest sites (`is_active`, and `requires_secret` ↔ `secret_state`, both unable to be DDL constraints because `CHECK` cannot reference another table) are named as weakest rather than quietly listed.\n- [x] Nullability stated per column, per backend family, with \"absent\" single-valued: NULL means absent, `''` is invalid, enforced by named `CHECK` constraints.\n- [x] Error sentinels enumerated with trigger conditions; translation by structured error codes plus constraint names defined in our own DDL, never message text.\n- [x] Out-of-scope list numbered, each item naming why and whom to flag.\n- [x] Counter-intuitive behaviours warned before a reader meets them.\n- [x] Contract carries no `.go` or `.sql` file — Go-shaped prose only.\n\n**Depends on:** Stories 1 and 2 (LT-14, LT-15). **Blocks:** Story 6 / LT-19 — the migration series creates this contract's tables, so migrations depend on the contract and not the reverse; 03's DAO implementation story (LT-35).\n**Model/effort:** opus/high — asymmetric risk: a wrong nullability or interface signature propagates into 03 and 04 and is expensive to reverse (`../02-ai-security-architecture/planning-approach.md` §1)\n\n> Corrected after transcription. This line originally read \"Stories 1, 2, 6\", which made the migration approach block the contract. It was wrong in both membership and direction, and it is a stale reference carried out of `../PLAN.md` story S1 — where \"S4\" named the migration approach under the pre-backlog numbering. The contract never consumed it. Noted rather than silently fixed because the error survived a plan approval, four debates and three cold reads before a literal transcription into Jira exposed it: every reviewer was reading the documents, and nobody's review was scoped to read the dependency graph.\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 3 — done."
  }
}

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "issueIdOrKey": "LT-50",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "fields": {
    "description": "**Description.** The cross-track consistency pass (F21) found that `pii-governance.md` specified a bulk retention sweep and a subject-deletion request sharing one code path, each writing a `deletion_log` row, and `multi-db-strategy.md` §5 defined the table — but no method on the interface could reach any of it. `Profiles().Delete` wrote no log row, and §3 forbids 03 from opening a transaction to combine the two, so a policy this track ruled on could not be implemented against the contract this track wrote, and no track owned the gap. Fixed by adding two composite-level methods in `multi-db-strategy.md` §3c: `DeleteExpired(ctx, class, olderThan, maxRows) (SweepResult, error)` and `DeleteProfile(ctx, id, externalRef)`, both writing `deletion_log` in the same transaction as the delete (signatures as finalized after 03's review — batched, and with `reason` asserted by the method rather than passed by the caller). `SweepResult` returns rows examined, rows deleted, and the age of the oldest surviving row — the last being the only signal that detects a silently stopped sweep, since rows-deleted cannot distinguish a broken sweep from an empty one.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] Both methods sit on the composite, not on a sub-repository — they span `user_profile` and `deletion_log`, and the DAO is the only layer permitted to open a transaction.\n- [x] One retention class per call; never a mixed-class predicate.\n- [x] Each class uses its own clock column — `created_at` for orphans, because a clock the read path touches lets a row reset its own expiry.\n- [x] `OldestSurvivingAt` returned from the DAO rather than left for 04 to compute, since only the DAO can answer it in the same query plan.\n- [x] `Profiles().Delete` deliberately still writes no log row, with the reason recorded.\n- [x] The complete set of cross-table operations is stated as three; a fourth requires a contract change.\n- [x] 03 accepted the addendum after a Detail Hawk first-pass review that raised four findings, all accepted: `OldestSurvivingAt`'s nil case narrowed to \"class is empty\" only (three conditions had been collapsing into it, including the two the metric exists to distinguish); `RetentionClass` zero value given an explicit conformance assertion; `reason` removed as a parameter on `DeleteProfile` and asserted by the method, since a caller-supplied reason code makes an audit trail's reasons caller-assertable; and `DeleteExpired` bounded by a required `maxRows` with one transaction per batch, never one per sweep, plus a never-request-scoped-context requirement.\n- [x] An interaction between two of those fixes, raised by neither, caught at ruling: batching makes deletable rows remain mid-sweep by construction, so `OldestSurvivingAt` would be old on every batch but the last and would fire the alert every run. It is therefore meaningful only when `Drained` is true. Two individually correct fixes would have shipped a flapping alert; a health signal that cries wolf gets muted, at which point it is not a health signal. Relayed to 04 so the alert rule is drained-gated.\n\n**Depends on:** Story 3 (LT-16), Story 5 (LT-18). **Blocks:** 03's S11 — the sweep-invocation and subject-deletion-request code that calls `DeleteExpired`/`DeleteProfile` and surfaces `OldestSurvivingAt` to 04's observability (LT-44).\n**Model/effort:** opus/high (contract addendum) + sonnet (03's first-pass review)\n\n> Ownership of the sweep job, resolved. The pass found that no track owned writing it: the contract made it writable, 03 had no such story, and `pii-governance.md` gave 04 only where jobs run. Renata claimed it as 03's S11 on 2026-09-12. The boundary is now three-way and clean — 05 defines the methods and what the metrics mean, 03 writes the code that calls them, 04 decides where it runs and reads the metrics. That was the orphan; it is no longer one.\n\nSource: 05-data-ops/backlog.md Story 8 — done."
  }
}

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "issueIdOrKey": "LT-39",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "fields": {
    "description": "**Description.** The client-facing handlers in `internal/api` implementing the assignment's Q2 (search and retrieve `user_profile`), built against S2's interfaces (fakes stand in for a real backend per `decisions/test-double-strategy.md`, so this doesn't wait on S3/S4). Implements the object-level `authorize(sub, scope, target)` call as an explicit in-handler step, not a second middleware, per the ruling in `handoff-03-auth.md` v3 (my own answer, confirmed by 02).\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [ ] Implements `handoff-03-auth.md` v3's scope vocabulary and pagination/rate-limit numbers without re-deriving 02's authz-scoping reasoning.\n- [ ] `authorize()` runs as an explicit call inside each handler after request parsing, before the DAO call — enforcement site: handler code structure, per the go-layout-debate.md-adjacent ruling recorded in this track's reply to 02. `authorize()` checks the `caller_referral`/caller-role data against the token-issuer's own datastore, not against 05's schema — 05 was never assigned that table (`handoff-03-auth.md` v3, F8).\n- [ ] `profile:search` responses carry masked PII fields by default (e.g. phone as `***-***-1234`, address reduced to `locality`/`region` only); unmasked detail requires a separate, separately-audited follow-up call under `profile:read:own` or `profile:read:any` against the specific record id — enforcement site: the search-response serialization path, distinct from the read-response one (`handoff-03-auth.md` v3, resolves F6).\n- [ ] Cursor-based pagination only, default page size 20, hard ceiling 50 — enforcement site: the pagination parameter parsing, rejecting any offset-based parameter. The handler's 20/50 is the authoritative clamp, enforced before the DAO is ever called — the DAO's own `Limit` bound (1..100, default 50 per `multi-db-strategy.md`) is a second, independent backstop only reachable if the handler clamp is bypassed, not a second policy a caller can rely on (consistency-pass F10: no document previously said which of the two governs).\n- [ ] A search request with no filter field at all is rejected by this handler before it reaches the DAO — the DAO itself treats an all-nil `ProfileQuery` as legal (`multi-db-strategy.md`), so this handler-layer rejection is the only enforcement site for \"no bare unconstrained search\" (consistency-pass F10, other half owned by 02 in `handoff-03-auth.md`).\n- [ ] A `profile:search` query is rejected outright, not truncated, if it would exceed the result cap unconstrained (e.g. a bare wildcard) — enforcement site: this handler's query-validation step, per `handoff-03-auth.md` v3's scope table (consistency-pass F52).\n- [ ] Unmapped DAO errors never surface `err.Error()` to the client; only the mapped sentinels' safe messages do — enforcement site: the boundary translation function from `decisions/error-semantics.md`. Authn failures (missing/invalid token) return 401; scope failures and `authorize()` policy denials both return 403 with an identical client body, distinguished only in the audit log (`decisions/error-semantics.md`, consistency-pass F7).\n- [ ] `profile:read:any` requests carry a `reason_code` from the closed enum on every call, logged with the audit record.\n- [ ] When `api-service` calls `idp-connector` on a caller's behalf, it obtains a `connector:identity-lookup`-scoped token first, using its own `CONNECTOR_CLIENT_ID`/`CONNECTOR_CLIENT_SECRET` credential (`PLANNING.md` config surface) — enforcement site: this handler-side outbound-client code, distinct from S8's idp-connector-side handlers, which only validate that token, not issue or hold this credential.\n\n**Depends on:** S2; **02: Auth scheme and authorization hand-off** (`handoff-03-auth.md` v3, accepted).\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 03-engineering-delivery/backlog.md S6 — open."
  }
}

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "issueIdOrKey": "LT-40",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "fields": {
    "description": "**Description.** The middleware at the `cmd/api-service` edge validating the client-credentials JWT scheme from `handoff-03-auth.md` v3 — public-key-only verification, `sub`/`scope`/`exp`/`iat`/`aud` claim checks, `kid`-based key rotation, no denylist (TTL-only revocation, a deliberate trade-off not to be re-litigated). Also covers the `APP_MODE=verifier|issuer` split (`PLANNING.md`) — this Deployment mode never mounts the signing key regardless of `APP_MODE`'s value, since `verifier` is this story's own code path and `issuer` is a separate mode of the same binary the F13 fix depends on to keep the two isolated by Deployment, not just by RBAC.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [ ] Implements 02's token scheme without re-deriving the no-refresh/no-denylist reasoning in `api-auth-design.md`.\n- [ ] Rejects any token whose `aud` doesn't match this service's audience — enforcement site: the claim-validation step, with a unit test using a mismatched-audience token.\n- [ ] Verifies with the public key only; the private signing key never touches this binary's code path — enforcement site: dependency/import check (no signing-key material referenced in `internal/api`).\n- [ ] Pins the expected signing algorithm and rejects any token whose header claims a different one, including `alg: none` and a symmetric-algorithm downgrade using the public key as an HMAC secret (RFC 8725 §3.1) — enforcement site: explicit algorithm check in the JWT verification call, not left to the library's default (`handoff-03-auth.md` v3 names this as a common library footgun).\n- [ ] The token-issuing endpoint (the `APP_MODE=issuer` mode) has its own failed-grant rate limiting and progressive backoff per `client_id` and per source IP, separate from the resource-API limits below, with alerting on a sustained run of failed grants against one `client_id` — enforcement site: issuer-mode middleware, distinct from the verifier-mode rate limiter (`handoff-03-auth.md` v3).\n- [ ] Per-client-credential rate limits (60 req/min read, 10 req/min search) and the cumulative distinct-record-touch counter (rolling 24h) are enforced and alert on sustained near-limit usage, not just throttle — enforcement site: the rate-limit middleware plus its own test.\n- [ ] The deadline budget for a request (context propagation into the DAO layer) is sized to cover realistic p99 DAO latency, per `decisions/context-propagation.md`'s ruling — stated as a concrete number in this story's implementation, not left as \"some deadline.\"\n\n**Depends on:** S1; **02: Auth scheme and authorization hand-off** (`handoff-03-auth.md` v3, accepted); **04: `APP_MODE` Deployment split** (`containerization-design.md`, F13).\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 03-engineering-delivery/backlog.md S7 — open."
  }
}

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "issueIdOrKey": "LT-41",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "fields": {
    "description": "**Description.** `cmd/idp-connector`'s outbound client and inbound handlers for the assignment's fixed `/auth` and `/identity` contracts, per `connector-security.md`'s no-cache-by-default token lifecycle (fetch per `/identity` call, discard on return; fresh isolated `Authorization` header per outbound request, never inherited from pooling/keep-alive; fetch → use-once → zeroize, retries re-fetch via `/auth`). Includes the connector's own inbound self-auth (distinct audience `idp-connector-service`, scope `connector:identity-lookup`, restricted to `api-service` as caller) per `handoff-03-auth.md` v3 §\"Where it's validated\" (Ingrid's S8 catch), and the `context.WithTimeout` + bounded pool + backoff requirement from `decisions/go-layout-debate.md`.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [ ] Implements 02's token-lifecycle spec (`connector-security.md`, `decisions/connector-token-lifecycle-redblue.md`) without re-litigating the no-cache-by-default posture.\n- [ ] No vendor token is persisted or cached across requests by default; if a future exception is ever justified it requires re-review, not a silent default change — enforcement site: no storage/cache call in the token-fetch path.\n- [ ] Every outbound vendor call sets `context.WithTimeout`; the outbound HTTP client uses a bounded connection pool; token-refresh retries back off rather than tight-looping — enforcement site: the HTTP client construction plus a test asserting a timeout fires.\n- [ ] The connector's own `/auth`/`/identity` handlers validate an inbound JWT with `aud: idp-connector-service` and `scope: connector:identity-lookup`, distinct from `api-service`'s audience — enforcement site: this handler's own middleware instance, with a test asserting a `loginid-api-service`-audience token is rejected here.\n- [ ] Never logs, in any environment or error path: the end-user's vendor password, any vendor `access_token` or full `Authorization` header value, or raw vendor error response bodies (per `handoff-04-secrets.md`'s never-log list) — enforcement site: log-call review against that list.\n\n**Depends on:** S1; **02: Connector security spec** (`connector-security.md`, accepted); **02: Auth scheme and authorization hand-off** (`handoff-03-auth.md` v3, accepted, for the connector's own self-auth).\n**Model/effort:** opus, high — the only implementation seat at this tier, per `planning-approach.md`'s connector-token-lifecycle exception.\n\nSource: 03-engineering-delivery/backlog.md S8 — open."
  }
}

118	---
119	
120	## Story 7 — Address cross-track consistency pass findings (LT-13)
121	
122	**Description:** The Phase 3 cross-track consistency pass (`decisions/cross-track-consistency.md`, F1–F50) named Naomi owner on four findings. F2 — the connector rationale's contract summary told 03 to build a two-method interface (`Authenticate`/`FetchIdentity`) whose token crosses the caller boundary, contradicting 02's rule that the vendor token never leaves the adapter; fixed by making both methods internal to the adapter behind one exported identity-lookup call. F33 — the framing claimed passkey extensibility "without changing the table shape," contradicting the accepted schema (no public-key/credential-id columns exist); fixed by rewording to "without changing the `method` discriminator," matching what `industry-framing.md` actually needs to claim. F9 — `personas-use-cases.md` required partial-match search on both name and phone, contradicting 05's accepted exact-only phone contract; resolved directly with Priya Nandakumar (05), two-party per `planning-approach.md` §2 (`decisions/f9-phone-search-ruling.md`) — phone stays exact-after-E.164-normalization, name partial-match unaffected, UX toggle scoped to name only. F48 — the three `decisions/*.md` files lacked the `CASTING.md` §5 model-and-turns footer; appended to all three. F3 (vendor-token ambiguity between 01's UX and 02's connector design) named Marcus as owner; 01 applied his exact sentence to `ux-notes.md:27` verbatim, unchanged.
123	
124	**Acceptance criteria:**
125	- [x] F2 fixed: `api-connector-design-rationale.md`'s contract summary now states the two-method shape is the adapter's internal interface, with one exported identity-lookup operation, so the vendor token never crosses the adapter boundary — consistent with `../02-ai-security-architecture/connector-security.md`.
126	- [x] F33 fixed: `industry-framing.md`:36 and `api-connector-design-rationale.md`:13 both now say "without changing the `method` discriminator" (method-specific columns/side table arrive by migration), not "without changing the table shape."
127	- [x] F9 fixed: `personas-use-cases.md`'s search-authorization appendix states phone as exact-match-after-normalization with reasoning and enforcement site named; `ux-notes.md`'s search screen scopes the partial-match toggle to name only; ruling recorded in `decisions/f9-phone-search-ruling.md`.
128	- [x] F48 fixed: `decisions/claims-audit.md`, `decisions/password-baseline-debate.md`, and `decisions/rationale-cold-read.md` each end with a model-and-turns footer.
129	- [x] F3 fixed: Marcus's exact sentence appended to `ux-notes.md:27`, stating the token is held only by the onboarding flow, only for the span between the two calls, never persisted past the signup step, citing `../02-ai-security-architecture/connector-security.md` §1.
130	
131	**Depends on:** Cross-track consistency pass (root, Phase 3) — Dana Whitfield; F9 resolved directly with 05 (Priya); F3 resolved with 02 (Marcus) supplying the exact wording.
132	**Model/effort:** sonnet, medium (lead-authored fixes; one direct two-party exchange with 05; one verbatim sentence applied from 02)
133	**Type:** Story
134	**Labels:** `track-01`, `from-consistency-pass`, `no-code-yet`
135	**Status:** Closed — all 5 assigned findings resolved (F2 corrected during the consistency-pass re-run per the addendum in `decisions/rationale-cold-read.md`).

2	
3	Lead: Marcus Ilori. Epic: **02 AI Architecture & Security Architecture** (Jira key: LT-2). Format per `../PLAN.md` Phase 4. All eleven stories from `PLAN.md` are listed in dependency order; ten are done (marked below) and shown as-run, not rewritten as if planned in hindsight — an honest backlog shows the work. S11 is the one open story, gated on Warren's implementation go-ahead.

Every later pattern run in this track (S3, S4, S5, S8) executed under this ratified catalog. See `PLAN.md` §0 for the full reasoning.

48	## S3 — Red/blue: connector token lifecycle (LT-23)
49	
50	**Status: done.**
51	
52	**Description:** Ran the ratified red/blue pattern (S1) against the IDP connector's vendor-token handling in `connector-security.md` §1: Tomasz Wrede's ranked top-five attack leaves, Felix Adebayo's alternatives turn (deleting two leaves by design change — no-cache-by-default rather than an encrypted, TTL-bound cache), Helena Marsh's blue response, Tomasz's rebuttal turn (closing a connection-reuse variant and tightening the accepted-replay-risk boundary). Full record: `decisions/connector-token-lifecycle-redblue.md`; attack-tree table appended to `connector-security.md`. This is the requirement set 03's connector implementation builds against directly.
53	
54	**Acceptance criteria:**
55	- [x] The receiving track (03) can implement the connector's token handling without re-deriving this run's reasoning — confirmed by Renata Cole directly.
56	- [x] "No persistent token cache by default" — enforcement site: the connector's HTTP client construction, one fetch-per-`/identity`-call code path, no cache read/write call in the default path.
57	- [x] "Fresh, isolated `Authorization` header per outbound request" — enforcement site: the outbound HTTP client factory used for vendor calls, explicitly not sharing a request-context object across calls.
58	- [x] "Fetch → use → zeroize, retries re-fetch" — enforcement site: the token variable's scope inside the single vendor-call function; a retry path that calls `/auth` again rather than reusing a held token.
59	- [x] Residual risk (bearer-token replay, accepted) is named in the artifact, not left implicit.

79	- [x] `profile:read:any` requires a `reason_code` from a closed enum on every call — enforcement site: request validation inside the same `authorize()` call, rejecting a missing or out-of-enum value.

81	- [x] Cursor-based pagination, page ceiling 50 — enforcement site: pagination-parameter validation in the handler layer.
82	- [x] Per-client rate limits (60/10 req/min) and the cumulative distinct-record-touch counter, applying to `read:any` regardless of `reason_code` presence — enforcement site: rate-limiting middleware plus a counting store keyed per client credential, incremented per distinct record id returned.

116	## S6 — Hand-off 02→03: auth scheme, validation point, authorization requirements (LT-26)
117	
118	**Status: done** (`handoff-03-auth.md`, now v3).
119	
120	**Description:** Synthesized S4's ruling and the token-shape decisions in `api-auth-design.md` into a receiver-shaped hand-off Renata Cole can build against without re-deriving this track's reasoning: token scheme, where it's validated, the final scope vocabulary and object-level policy hook, pagination/rate-limit numbers, the audit-log field list, and an explicit "not yours to decide" list. Revised to v2 after S8's independent review surfaced two implementation-relevant fixes (the decomposition counter's scope-coverage gap; the connector's own inbound-auth requirement), then to v3 after the cross-track consistency pass resolved six further findings (F3, F5, F6, F8, F10, F-pag, F52) that touched this hand-off. Accepted by 03 with a confirmed `authorize()` placement (in-handler, not middleware) and `DB_DSN_FILE` folded into the config surface.
121	
122	**Acceptance criteria:**
123	- [x] Receiving track (03) can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning in `api-auth-design.md`/`connector-security.md` — confirmed by Renata directly, cold read "clean."
124	- [x] Token TTL (5–15 min), no refresh, no denylist — enforcement site: `exp` claim check in the verification middleware; absence of a refresh-grant or denylist-lookup code path.
125	- [x] Verifier pins expected algorithm, rejects `alg: none`/downgrade — enforcement site: explicit algorithm allow-list parameter on the JWT verification call.
126	- [x] Public-key-only verification in `api-service`; private key isolated to the issuing code path — enforcement site: Kubernetes RBAC Role (per `handoff-04-secrets.md` row #2) plus code-level separation between issuing and verifying functions.
127	- [x] `idp-connector`'s own `/auth`/`/identity` require authentication with a distinct audience/scope — enforcement site: the same JWT middleware pattern applied to `idp-connector`'s router, configured with `aud: idp-connector-service`.

141	## S7 — Hand-off 02→04: secrets inventory and never-log list (LT-27)
142	
143	**Status: done** (`handoff-04-secrets.md`, now v2).
144	
145	**Description:** Authored the secrets inventory and never-log list Theo Bergman's track needs to design secrets delivery against, then ran Ingrid Solano's single objection turn (S7's assigned pattern — one turn, not a full debate) and folded in all four accepted objections: the authorization-server's ownership was mis-scoped by omission, a KMS-access credential row was missing, the `DB_DSN` env-var exception was too weak, and audit-log read access needed its own RBAC line distinct from Secret access. Cold-read by 04's Newcomer (Wesley Okonkwo) caught two further gating gaps (TOTP/token-cache feature-status ambiguity; a non-self-contained trust-boundary reference), both fixed.
146	
147	**Acceptance criteria:**
148	- [x] Receiving track (04) can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning in `threat-model.md`/`api-auth-design.md`/`connector-security.md` — confirmed by 04's Newcomer cold read, two gating items fixed before acceptance.
149	- [x] `DB_DSN_FILE` required as the primary delivery mechanism, `DB_DSN` a transitional fallback — enforcement site: the config-loading code in `internal/config`, preferring the file path when both are set (confirmed folded into 03's Service boundaries).
150	- [x] JWT signing private key file-mount only, RBAC-restricted to the issuing code path's service account — enforcement site: the Kubernetes Role scoping `get`/`list` on that Secret.
151	- [x] Client secrets stored hashed (Argon2id), never plaintext at rest — enforcement site: the provisioning code path that writes the hash, per `threat-model.md` Asset 1.
152	- [x] One `Secret` per vendor registration (ABC/XYZ never share a Secret) — enforcement site: the Kubernetes manifest's per-vendor Secret object.
153	- [x] Never-log list (vendor password, vendor token, PII values, raw vendor error bodies, signing key, JWTs, client secrets, `DB_DSN`, full `/auth`/`/identity` bodies, PII-bearing query params) — enforcement site: a log-formatting/redaction layer that structurally cannot emit these fields, not a code-review convention alone.
154	- [x] Audit-log read access is a distinct, narrower grant than Secret-read access — enforcement site: log-pipeline RBAC or a separate log-sink access control, 04's mechanism.
155	
156	**Depends on:** one Skeptic objection turn (no debate pattern)

Result: Helena reviewed `threat-model.md` (4 citation/precision fixes, 1 completeness note), Tomasz Wrede reviewed `api-auth-design.md` (4 findings, including a decomposition-counter gap that made a rate limit a silent no-op for `profile:read:any`), Ingrid Solano reviewed `connector-security.md` (2 findings — no auth requirement on inbound calls to the connector; no stated assumption about what a vendor token authorizes). All ten findings accepted, zero declined. Full record: `decisions/second-review-security-docs.md`.

Revised to v2 after S8's independent review surfaced two implementation-relevant fixes (the decomposition counter's scope-coverage gap; the connector's own inbound-auth requirement), then to v3 after the cross-track consistency pass resolved six further findings (F3, F5, F6, F8, F10, F-pag, F52) that touched this hand-off. Accepted by 03 with a confirmed `authorize()` placement (in-handler, not middleware) and `DB_DSN_FILE` folded into the config surface.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n- [x] Receiving track (03) can act on this without re-deriving the reasoning in `api-auth-design.md`/`connector-security.md` — confirmed by Renata directly, cold read \"clean.\"\n- [x] Token TTL (5–15 min), no refresh, no denylist — enforcement site: `exp` claim check in the verification middleware; absence of a refresh-grant or denylist-lookup code path.\n- [x] Verifier pins expected algorithm, rejects `alg: none`/downgrade — enforcement site: explicit algorithm allow-list parameter on the JWT verification call.\n- [x] Public-key-only verification in `api-service`; private key isolated to the issuing code path — enforcement site: Kubernetes RBAC Role (per `handoff-04-secrets.md` row #2) plus code-level separation between issuing and verifying functions.\n- [x] `idp-connector`'s own `/auth`/`/identity` require authentication with a distinct audience/scope — enforcement site: the same JWT middleware pattern applied to `idp-connector`'s router, configured with `aud: idp-connector-service`.\n- [x] Token-endpoint brute-force protection — enforcement site: rate limiter on the token-issuing endpoint, keyed by `client_id` + source IP.\n- [x] Audit-log field list (`sub`, scope, record id, `reason_code`, policy decision, timestamp, outcome) and nothing beyond it — enforcement site: a single structured-logging call at the end of each search/retrieve handler, not scattered `log.Printf` calls a reviewer has to hunt for.\n\n**Depends on:** S4.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high (lead synthesis, no new hire turns); sonnet, high for 03's implementation against it.\n\nSource: 02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md S6 — done."
  }
}

Stand up the Go module and the two-binary skeleton the org already committed to in `PLANNING.md`'s Service boundaries section: `cmd/api-service`, `cmd/idp-connector`, both thin wrappers over a shared `internal/app` bootstrap package (route registration, config wiring) per `decisions/go-layout-debate.md`. `internal/config` loads the env-var surface named in `PLANNING.md` (`DB_DRIVER`, `DB_DSN`/`DB_DSN_FILE`, `HTTP_ADDR`, `AUTH_JWT_ISSUER`/`AUTH_JWT_AUDIENCE`, `IDP_ABC_*`). Stub handlers only — no DAO, no auth, no connector logic yet; this story's job is a buildable skeleton other stories attach to.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[ \\] The receiving track (04, reading this for containerization) can act on the resulting layout without re-deriving the reasoning in `PLANNING.md` or `decisions/go-layout-debate.md`.\n* \\[ \\] Both `cmd/*/main.go` are thin wrappers over `internal/app`; no route-registration or config-loading logic duplicated between them — enforcement site: code review against `decisions/go-layout-debate.md`'s ruling.\n* \\[ \\] `internal/config` loads every variable named in `PLANNING.md`'s Service boundaries section, with `DB_DSN_FILE` taking precedence over `DB_DSN` when both are set — enforcement site: a config-loading unit test asserting precedence.\n* \\[ \\] Module builds and both binaries start (against stub handlers) with no real backend configured.\n\n**Depends on:** none.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 03-engineering-delivery/backlog.md S1 — open.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10155","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"In Dev","id":"10155","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/4","id":4,"key":"indeterminate","colorName":"yellow","name":"In Progress"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-34"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"unknown","toolName":"transitionJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"6cbef92a-3d9e-496c-8263-e1901b5fb780","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}

No backend logic yet — this is the shape both backend packages implement against, plus the fakes S9's tests use per `decisions/test-double-strategy.md`.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[ \\] A hire or reviewer unfamiliar with 05's reasoning can implement a backend against this package without re-reading `multi-db-strategy.md` — the Go types here are the contract, not a paraphrase of it.\n* \\[ \\] Every sentinel in 05's §4 is defined verbatim (name and wrapped message), including `ErrAlreadyExists`'s status as an internal-error signal with no caller-reachable path — enforcement site: `dao` package source, doc comment on `ErrAlreadyExists` stating that status explicitly (per Oren's finding #1, ruled by 05).\n* \\[ \\] `CreateProfileWithCredential(ctx, p, c)` exists on the composite per 05's §3b resolution, with `c.UserID` ignored on input — enforcement site: method signature plus a unit test asserting the input `UserID` is overwritten.\n* \\[ \\] Pointer fields follow \"absent, never empty\" — a non-nil, empty `*string` is rejected as `ErrInvalidArgument` at the boundary, not silently accepted — enforcement site: input-validation unit test per field.\n\n**Depends on:** S1; **05: DAO Go-shaped contract** (`multi-db-strategy.md`, stable, accepted).\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 03-engineering-delivery/backlog.md S2 — open.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10155","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"In Dev","id":"10155","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/4","id":4,"key":"indeterminate","colorName":"yellow","name":"In Progress"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-35"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"unknown","toolName":"transitionJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"d43c34c4-6c67-4f87-9898-31c92a3715fb","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "issueIdOrKey": "LT-2",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "fields": {
    "description": "**Track lead:** Marcus Ilori (persona; own Claude Code session `02-ai-security-architecture-a2`).\n\n**Owns:** the AI-tooling/workflow narrative for the whole submission; threat model for credential storage, PII exposure, and third-party token handling; API authentication/authorization design (OAuth2 client-credentials, short-lived JWT, scoped authz); connector token-lifecycle security; the receiver-shaped hand-offs to 03 (auth) and 04 (secrets inventory + never-log list); independent second review of security-graded surfaces.\n\n**Planning outputs (complete through S10):** `02-ai-security-architecture/PLAN.md`; `threat-model.md`, `api-auth-design.md`, `connector-security.md`, `ai-workflow-narrative.md`, `planning-approach.md` (+ appendices), `handoff-03-auth.md` v2, `handoff-04-secrets.md` v1; decisions `connector-token-lifecycle-redblue.md` (no-cache-by-default vendor token), `search-authz-scoping.md`, `ai-workflow-claim-debate.md`, `second-review-security-docs.md` (10 accepted findings).\n\n**Stories** are authored by the lead in `02-ai-security-architecture/backlog.md` and transcribed here by the PM. S11 (post-implementation review) is gated on the code go-ahead.\n\n**Repository:** https://github.com/wtvamp/loginid-takehome"
  }
}

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "issueIdOrKey": "LT-3",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "fields": {
    "description": "**Track lead:** Renata Cole (persona; own Claude Code session `03-engineering-delivery-b7`).\n\n**Owns:** the Go code for all three assignment questions — the multi-database DAO (PostgreSQL/CockroachDB, SQLite) behind a composite `dao.Repository` (`Profiles()`/`Credentials()`/`Methods()`), the REST search/retrieve API with auth middleware per 02's hand-off, the IDP connector (`/auth`, `/identity`) per 02's connector-security design, test strategy, README. Two binaries: `cmd/api-service`, `cmd/idp-connector`. Service boundaries are published in `PLANNING.md`.\n\n**Planning outputs (complete):** `03-engineering-delivery/PLAN.md`; decisions `go-layout-debate.md`, `error-semantics.md`, `context-propagation.md`, `test-double-strategy.md`. Inputs accepted: `02/handoff-03-auth.md` v2 and `05/multi-db-strategy.md` S1 contract (after Detail Hawk first-pass review).\n\n**Gate:** no implementation code exists or is written until Warren's explicit project-wide go-ahead. Stories are authored by the lead in `03-engineering-delivery/backlog.md` and transcribed here by the PM; each implementation story must point at a stable contract.\n\n**Repository:** https://github.com/wtvamp/loginid-takehome"
  }
}

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "issueIdOrKey": "LT-4",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "fields": {
    "description": "**Track lead:** Theo Bergman (persona; own Claude Code session `04-infra-devops-47`).\n\n**Owns:** containerization design (distroless multi-stage Go builds; Kubernetes manifest sketch targeting the lab cluster as a design-only reference — nothing deployed, operator never contacted), CI pipeline (lint, build, race tests, govulncheck, Trivy on merge, CockroachDB test job), local dev loop (compose with Postgres/CockroachDB profiles, SQLite as zero-dependency path), secrets delivery implementing 02's inventory row by row (`DB_DSN_FILE` precedence), observability with never-log enforcement and the retention-sweep metrics from 05.\n\n**Planning outputs (complete):** `04-infra-devops/PLAN.md`; `containerization-design.md`, `ci-pipeline.md`, `local-dev-loop.md`, `secrets-delivery.md`, `observability.md`; `decisions/newcomer-coldread-boundaries-secrets.md`. Inputs: 03 service boundaries, 02 secrets hand-off, 05 final migration approach.\n\n**Gate:** real Dockerfiles/CI/compose artifacts wait for Warren's code go-ahead. Stories are authored by the lead in `04-infra-devops/backlog.md` and transcribed here by the PM.\n\n**Repository:** https://github.com/wtvamp/loginid-takehome"
  }
}

{
  "cloudId": "db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176",
  "issueIdOrKey": "LT-5",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "fields": {
    "description": "**Track lead:** Priya Nandakumar (persona; own Claude Code session `data-ops-planning-phase`, Opus for the planning phase on asymmetric-risk grounds).\n\n**Owns:** schema for `user_profile` / `user_credential` with an `auth_method` lookup table, the multi-database abstraction strategy (per-driver implementations, engine-aware retry seam for CockroachDB SQLSTATE 40001, conformance suite across every backend), the Go-shaped DAO contract that 03 implements against, migration approach for 04 (single-runner requirement; CRDB `pg_try_advisory_lock` silently no-ops), PII retention windows and deletion mechanism.\n\n**Planning outputs (complete):** `05-data-ops/PLAN.md`; `multi-db-strategy.md` (S1 contract, accepted by 03), `migration-approach.md` (final, delivered to 04), `pii-governance.md`; research `research-cockroachdb-postgres-semantics.md`; decisions `multi-db-abstraction.md`, `search-query-shape.md` (8/8 objections accepted, four live defects) and the cold-read records. Org-wide principle adopted from this track: every caller-visible guarantee names an enforcement site.\n\n**Stories** are authored by the lead in `05-data-ops/backlog.md` and transcribed here by the PM.\n\n**Repository:** https://github.com/wtvamp/loginid-takehome"
  }
}

Includes the `crdb.ExecuteTx`-style retry wrapper on every write (CockroachDB stays at SERIALIZABLE per 05's ruling — READ COMMITTED was considered and rejected), SQLSTATE-plus-our-own-constraint-name error translation, and the transactional `CreateProfileWithCredential`.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[ \\] Implements against S2's interfaces with no re-derivation of 05's schema or error-translation reasoning.\n* \\[ \\] Every write (`Create`, `Update`, `Upsert`, `Delete`, `CreateProfileWithCredential`) runs through the retry wrapper — enforcement site: the wrapper is the single call path every write method uses, verified by the conformance suite (S5) exercising a retryable condition against CockroachDB.\n* \\[ \\] Driver errors translate to sentinels by structured code (SQLSTATE) plus our own named DDL constraints, never free-text matching — enforcement site: the translation table in `multi-db-strategy.md` §4, one `switch`/lookup per condition, no `strings.Contains` on an error message anywhere in this package.\n* \\[ \\] `Upsert`'s `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` list explicitly excludes `created_at` — enforcement site: the SQL statement itself plus a unit test asserting `created_at` survives a re-hydration Upsert unchanged (per Oren's finding #3, ruled by 05).\n* \\[ \\] Fuzzy name search uses the `LOWER(name) LIKE ?` form matching the GIN expression index, with explicit `%`/`_`/`\\` escaping — enforcement site: query construction plus a unit test with a `%`-containing search term.\n\n**Depends on:** S2.\n**Model/effort:** sonnet, high.\n\nSource: 03-engineering-delivery/backlog.md S3 — Covers both binaries' Dockerfiles, resource requests/limits sized per service (CPU-bound `api-service` vs. I/O-bound `idp-connector`), the migration `Job` (parallelism 1, gated by the CI pipeline's exclusivity mechanism, not Kubernetes ordering alone), a default-deny `NetworkPolicy` on `idp-connector` so its \"no inbound Service\" isolation claim actually holds against the namespace's default-allow network, and — per the consistency pass's F13 finding — a **third manifest**: `api-service-issuer`, a second Deployment of the same `api-service` image (`APP_MODE=issuer`) whose own ServiceAccount is the only one that mounts the JWT signing key, since RBAC on the `Secret` verb does nothing once it's volume-mounted into the verifying Deployment's replicas.\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[ \\] The receiving track (whoever implements/reviews this) can act on the manifests without re-deriving the reasoning in `containerization-design.md`.\n* \\[ \\] Both images build from a pinned Go version, produce a static binary, and contain nothing but the binary (+ CA certs for `idp-connector`) — enforcement site: multi-stage Dockerfile's final `COPY` list.\n* \\[ \\] Neither Pod can write to its own root filesystem at runtime — enforcement site: `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`.\n* \\[ \\] `idp-connector` is unreachable except from `api-service` — enforcement site: the `NetworkPolicy` ingress rule scoped to `api-service`'s pod selector.\n* \\[ \\] A stuck `idp-connector` cannot starve `api-service` if colocated on one node — enforcement site: `resources.limits` on both Pod specs.\n* \\[ \\] The migration `Job` cannot start a second concurrent run — enforcement site: the CI pipeline's concurrency-gated deploy stage (Story 3), not a database lock.\n* \\[ \\] The JWT signing private key is mounted into `api-service-issuer` only, never into `api-service`'s own Deployment — enforcement site: `api-service`'s manifest carries no volume/mount referencing that `Secret` at all, verified by manifest inspection, not RBAC.\n\n**Depends on:** 03 — `cmd/api-service` and `cmd/idp-connector` build as real binaries (service boundaries already stable, per `PLANNING.md`); 05 — final migration tooling name for the `Job`'s invocation (already final, `05-data-ops/migration-approach.md`).\n**Model/effort:** Sonnet, medium.\n\nSource: 04-infra-devops/backlog.md Story 1 — The migration-job stage is where 05's R2 exclusivity requirement is actually enforced — a concurrency-gated pipeline stage, not a database lock, since no single lock mechanism covers both the right scope (session, to span `goose`'s per-file transactions) and the right engine (CockroachDB supports transaction-scope only).\n\n**Acceptance criteria**\n\n* \\[ \\] A developer or reviewer can act on this pipeline description without re-deriving why each stage exists.\n* \\[ \\] A lint or test failure blocks merge — enforcement site: required-status-check on the PR, not advisory.\n* \\[ \\] A CockroachDB-specific SQL incompatibility surfaces at PR time, not deploy time — enforcement site: the dedicated CockroachDB testcontainer job.\n* \\[ \\] Only one migration run can reach the migrate stage at a time, across concurrent deploys — enforcement site: the pipeline's own concurrency group/mutex on the deploy environment.\n* \\[ \\] No secret enters a build log or image layer — enforcement site: `gitleaks` stage plus the Dockerfile's minimal `COPY` list (Story 1).\n* \\[ \\] The final deploy stage is documented (which manifests, which namespace, which credential) but not invoked — enforcement site: stage exists as a named, non-executing step until a separate real-deploy decision is made.\n\n**Depends on:** 03 — test-strategy outline for `go test ./...` to run against; 05 — `migration-approach.md` (final).\n**Model/effort:** Sonnet, medium.\n\nSource: 04-infra-devops/backlog.md Story 3 — open.","assignee":null,"status":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/status/10155","description":"","iconUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/images/icons/statuses/generic.png","name":"In Dev","id":"10155","statusCategory":{"self":"https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176/rest/api/3/statuscategory/4","id":4,"key":"indeterminate","colorName":"yellow","name":"In Progress"}}},"webUrl":"https://uplifttech.atlassian.net/browse/LT-47"}]},"context":{"atlassianAccountId":"712020:117c11fc-72d8-4b64-8daa-b0d3c30448d0","cloudId":"db488eae-d6cb-4100-92a9-e7a4519fc176","clientName":"claude.ai","mcpClientName":"unknown","toolName":"transitionJiraIssue","endpoint":"v1:streamable-http","sessionId":"r11-071f2b46-97ed-469f-a9f4-dfc6c65ebfaf","invocationId":"d9a9b064-92a5-4601-9422-5b846d0cf587","env":"prod","featureFlags":{"mcp-app-v2-primary":false,"analytics-jira-mcp-app":true,"mcp-jira-instrumentation-phase-1":false,"ken-4811-4724-jira-mcp-status-assignee-fields":false,"jira-mcp-app-loading-skeleton-and-error-case":false}}}
